# Abilities

An ability is a unique skill of a hero that does damage, grants utility, or both. All heroes have 4 base abilities that are unlocked throughout the early stages of the game using ability unlocks, and upgraded via ability points. Abilities can be either active, passive, or partially passive, and will define how a hero plays, scales, builds and wins using a specific strategy.

## Ability unlocks

[edit | edit source]

Abilities are unlocked with  **Ability Unlocks** earned at  **600**,  **1200**,  **2100** and  **3600** soul thresholds (Boon levels 0, 2, 4 and 6). The first 3 non-ultimate abilities can be unlocked in any order, while the ultimate ability can only be unlocked at level 6. Ability unlocks cannot be refunded.

## Ability points

[edit | edit source]

 Infernus  Napalm showing the 3 levels of upgrades an ability can have, at 1, 2 and 5 points. (Upgrades may be outdated)

**Ability Points** are earned at every boon that does not give an ability unlock. These are used to upgrade the power of unlocked abilities, granting additional bonuses and better stats. All abilities have 3 tiers for upgrades, costing 1, 2, and 5 points to unlock. Unspent points are shown under the player's ability icons.

The player can refund an upgrade by clicking its slot up to 10 seconds after unlocking it, if they haven't used any abilities in that time window.

All 32 ability points can be earned by leveling up.

## Types of abilities

[edit | edit source]

Abilities come in three main categories: **active**, **passive**, and **partially passive**.

### Active

[edit | edit source]

Active abilities are abilities that are used by pressing the input key, and have a cooldown before they can be used again. An active ability is linked to a hero's power and when it is on cooldown gives a window of opportunity for counterplay (see strategy for more). Active abilities cannot be used if the player is under the effects of a stun, silence or displacement. Active abilities can have a range of properties including being instant, channeled or having charges.

An **instant** ability is an ability that can be used only once immediately before being put on cooldown. It is seen as the most basic and straightforward type of abilities. An example of an instant active ability is  Bebop's  Sticky Bomb. Some active abilities can be recast during a specific timeframe, such as  Mina's  Sanguine Retreat, but will still go on cooldown after the first use while the recast timer is active.

A **channeled** ability is an ability that requires channeling it for a duration, indicated by a filled bar slowly diminishing on the characters HUD. The channel can be stopped before the channel duration is complete, and will go on cooldown after it's first press before the channel duration has completed. Channeled abilities often prohibit the player from movement but this is not a rule. F. ex.  Kelvin's  Arctic Beam allows walking around though at a slowed movement speed and crouching, but not dashing and jumping (the jumping key is default the key to cancel channeling).  Dynamo's  Singularity blocks all movement inputs from the player while channeling. Channeled abilities can be stopped preemptively by and opponent by using a stun or interrupt, but a silence or displacement will not stop an ongoing channeled ability. This does not affect the cooldown of the ability.

An ability with charges, showing 3 ready charges on the left and 5 ready charges on the right.

A **charged** ability - or, an ability with **charges** - is an ability that can be used multiple times in a row, and has a separate cooldown for the time between charges and the time for a charge to be restored. This is indicated by a white bar over the ability icon on the players HUD, and is split by a thin black line for the amount of charges the ability currently possess. A charge that is currently on cooldown is indicated by a gray bar slowly filling up in place of the white bar. Some abilities will also start as instant active, and gain charges with levels. ### Passive

[edit | edit source]

A passive ability is an ability that is not directly activatable by the player, but by some condition of the game. Passive abilities can not be turned off or deactivated in any way after they have been unlocked. A passive ability can affect either the hero itself, such as  Abrams's  Infernal Resilience or an enemy hero such as  Infernus's  Afterburn, and heroes with a passive ability will often have this ability as a defining trait signifying how they are played and built.

The passive abilities in Deadlock are:

| Victor | Shocking Reanimation (Has a cooldown) |
| Vyper | Slither |

### Partial Passive

[edit | edit source]

Partial passive abilities are active abilities with passive components or a passive ability with an active trigger (and are therefore affected by silences, stuns, etc). These are:

- Billy's  Blasted which has a passive component of reloading ammo and marking enemies, but can be activated. The passive effect persists through the active cooldown.

- Mirage's  Djinn's Mark which can be activated early, but the mark will build and trigger even if silenced.
- Shiv's  Bloodletting has both deferring damage as a passive, and an active to clear said deferred damage.
- Victor's  Pain Battery where the damage storing is handled as a passive, but the actual usage of the ability behaves as an active ability.

## Ability Scaling and damage

[edit | edit source]

Abilities have three ways of being useful: dealing  spirit damage, dealing  melee damage or providing utility.

### Spirit Damage

[edit | edit source]

Spirit damage is the main form of ability damage there is in Deadlock, and the vast majority of abilities will deal all or some of its damage as  spirit damage. This damage is generally split into two parts: the **base damage** represented by an integer, and the **spirit scaling** **damage** represented by a percentage of the heros spirit power. The base damage is a base value that can only be changed via leveling up the ability using  **Ability Points**, the spririt scaling damage can be increased by obtaining more spirit power via items, golden statues, powerups or the rejuvenator. Please see the page on spirit power scaling for more details.

### Melee Damage

[edit | edit source]

**Melee damage** means that the ability will deal a percentage of the hero's current  melee damage on contact. This will also apply any effect currently attributed to the melee of the hero, such as  Spirit Strike or  Melee Lifesteal. Conversely, this also means the damage is reduced by a hero's melee damage resist from items like  Close Quarters. Some heroes can upgrade their abilities to instead apply heavy  melee damage, and this will apply item effects that benefit from this such as  Melee Charge. This will not, however, work with mechanics needing heavy melee attacks such as a sinner's sacrifice, powerup or a rejuvenator.

### Utility

[edit | edit source]

Some abilities will have no damage dealt, but will instead provide the hero with some sort of utility to use while playing. This is a wide topic and can be anything from  Calico's  Ava providing mobility and eventually health regeneration,  Mo & Krill's  Sand Blast providing a disarm status effect on enemies, and  Paige's  Plot Armor providing a barrier and weapon damage.

### Scaling

[edit | edit source]

While most abilities scale on spirit power, there are some that have alternate ways of scaling. These are  McGinnis's  Mini Turret whose health scales on her own maximum health, and  Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine which scales on her weapon damage. These are the only two abilities that scale on something other than spirit power.

A few abilities have no scaling at all, only increasing in power when spending  **Ability Points** to upgrade them. This includes  Lash's  Grapple,  Mo & Krill's  Sand Blast and  Grey Talon's  Rain of Arrows &  Spirit Snare to name a few.

Some abilities apply their spirit scaling not in increased damage, but in other aspects of how they work.  These vary wildly, and include  Lash's  Death Slam which increases its throwing range, and  McGinnis's  Medicinal Specter which extends its duration.

# Ability Cooldown

**Ability Cooldown** is the time it takes for an Ability to be usable again.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Charged Abilities
- 2 Calculation

- 2.1 Calculating Cooldown Reduction
- 3 Sources of Ability Cooldown Reduction

- 3.1 Map Spawns
- 4 Item Cooldown

- 4.1 Sources of Item Cooldown Reduction

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Cooldowns range from a few seconds, as in  Lady Geist's  Malice, to a few minutes, as in  Dynamo's  Singularity. Ability cooldowns can be reduced by acquiring the Cooldown Reduction stat, which reduces the cooldown by a percentage of base ability time.

### Charged Abilities

[edit | edit source]

Some abilities can acquire multiple charges. In those cases, the ability cooldown represents the time for a charge to become available again after being used. This should not be confused with the time between charges, which describes the delay after using a charge that a different charge can be used.

## Calculation

[edit | edit source]

### Calculating Cooldown Reduction

[edit | edit source]

Despite being presented in-game as +X% Cooldown Reduction, multiple sources stack **multiplicatively**, not additively:

Total Cooldown Reduction=1−(1−CR1)×(1−CR2)…

**Example:**
With **12%** Cooldown Reduction from  Diviner's Kevlar and **16%** from  Superior Cooldown:

1. Convert percentages to decimals: 0.12 and 0.16.
1. Subtract from 1: (1 - 0.12) = **0.88** and (1 - 0.16) = **0.84**.
1. Multiply the remainders: 0.88 × 0.84 = **0.7392**.
1. Subtract from 1: 1 - 0.7392 = **0.2608**.
1. Total Cooldown Reduction is approximately **26%**, not 28%.

### Map Spawns

[edit | edit source]

- Golden Statues have a chance to drop a permanent Cooldown Reduction buff.
- Powerup runes can provide a temporary Casting buff that provides +**12**% to +**20**% Cooldown Reduction for 160 seconds (scaling with game time from 5 to 40 minutes).

## Item Cooldown

[edit | edit source]

Item Cooldown is the time it takes for an Item to be usable again. This includes both Active and Passive items.

Charge-Up items such as  Tankbuster and  Mercurial Magnum are not affected by Item Cooldown Reduction.

# Ability Range

Shiv's Slice and Dice ability, improved by bonus Ability Range and Spirit Power stats.

Ability Range determines the effective distance and cast range of hero abilities. It is measured in a distance of meters, and stat gains are measured in percentages.

For example, Shiv's **Slice and Dice** ability has a dash range of **12 meters**. Purchasing Mystic Expansion improves this by **35%**, making the new effective dash range of the ability **16.2 meters**.

## Calculation

[edit | edit source]

### Calculating Ability Range

[edit | edit source]

Multiple sources of Ability Range stack **multiplicatively**, not additively:

Total Ability Range=1−(1−R1)×(1−R2)…

**Example:**
With **35%** from  Greater Expansion and **10%** from  Divine Barrier:

1. Convert percentages to decimals: 0.35 and 0.10.
1. Subtract from 1: (1 - 0.35) = **0.65** and (1 - 0.10) = **0.90**.
1. Multiply the remainders: 0.65 × 0.90 = **0.585**.
1. Subtract from 1: 1 - 0.585 = **0.415**.
1. Total Ability Range bonus is approximately **41.5%**, not 45%.

“

The only way to face a problem is head-on.

**Abrams** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. He is a hard-boiled, hard-hitting bruiser of a character that focuses on engaging groups of enemies and relying on his high health, high damage output, and life draining ability to stay in the fight. With a powerful area stun and a devastating shoulder charge, Abrams can isolate fragile targets from the rest of the team and set-up his more damaging allies to finish them off.

A capable and well-known detective of New York, Abrams solved crimes ranging from kidnappings to ritual murders. One day, a mysterious Tome was left on his desk with a note of "Don't let them have it" scrawled in Onyx blood; followed by car bombings and break-ins to his office. Now, Abrams is trying to figure out just what the hell is going on.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Abrams/Lore** for more story content.*

“

Hard hitting, hard headed, and hard drinking; Detective Abrams has been a fixture on the New York investigating scene for years.  From stolen art, to missing persons, to ritual murders; Abrams didn't just take any case that came across his desk... he solved them.

But his days of following cheating spouses came to an end the day he opened his office door and found The Tome sitting on his desk.

No instruction was left for him save for a brief note scrawled in onyx blood that read "Don't let them have it".  Abrams hasn't figured where the thing came from; but seeing as his home has been broken into, his office tossed on 3 different occasions, and his car firebombed he has a vested interest in figuring out what the hell is going on.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Abrams was named **Atlas** in *Neon Prime*, and also known as **Bull**. The icon for Infernal Resilience previously had a bull design.
- Abrams is voiced by Samoa Joe, a professional wrestler.[1]

- Haze may call Abrams a "juggernaut".[3] Samoa Joe voiced the character **Juggernaut** in the "Call of the Bladeform Legacy" arcana voice pack in *Dota 2*, and later in *Dota Underlords*.
- Abrams' Tome contains a ripped page matching Oathkeeper's sign.[4]
- The first version of Abrams' Tome in-game used textures from TF2's Bombinomicon.
- In *The Binding of Oathkeeper* artwork, Abrams has spikes on his back.
- Abrams was the only hero who had unique animations in the shop menu screen. These animations have been removed.
- Abrams was made slightly taller in an unlisted patch change around November 2024.
- Abrams' updated model was first leaked in the 2024-12-06 Update, and later removed. Compared to the final model, this version had slightly different facial hair and still had his old book model.
- "Investigating the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Abrams in the Hideout.

This book is dangerous. I can't let it fall into the wrong hands.

Hard hitting, hard headed, and hard drinking; Detective Abrams has been a fixture on the New York investigating scene for years.  From stolen art, to missing persons, to ritual murders; Abrams didn't just take any case that came across his desk... he solved them.

But his days of following cheating spouses came to an end the day he opened his office door and found The Tome sitting on his desk.

No instruction was left for him save for a brief note scrawled in onyx blood that read "Don't let them have it".  Abrams hasn't figured where the thing came from; but seeing as his home has been broken into, his office tossed on 3 different occasions, and his car firebombed he has a vested interest in figuring out what the hell is going on.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Abrams' goal in the ritual is to destroy the Tome.[1][2]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Abrams is Ixian.[3] He was likely born in Ixia and seems to speak their native language.[4][5] Unlike  Infernus, Abrams does not demonstrate control over fire. It's implied that Abrams didn't always live in New York, and it's unknown when he moved to the city.[4][6]

Abrams' office in *The Binding of Oathkeeper*

For years, Abrams was a skilled private detective and a fixture on the New York investigating scene, known for taking and solving any case that came across his desk.[7] Abrams' detective agency is called "Abrams Investigations", with the slogan "we specialize in the unknowable and unthinkable".[8] One of his cases in the past had him working alongside  Venator.[9] Abrams has also been investigating the Paradox Organisation.[10]

He lives in an apartment in New York, and his office can be seen in *The Binding of Oathkeeper.* Outside of work, Abrams is a regular at Jezebel's and plays in  Wraith's weekly poker game.[11][12][13]

When the Tome was left in his possession, Abrams' life suddenly turned upside down as his home and office were broken into on several occasions and his car was firebombed.[7] With his life at risk, Abrams stopped going to Jezebel's and Wraith's poker games to focus on finding out what the Tome is.[14][15]

Abrams' business card in *The Binding of Oathkeeper*

The Tome itself is shrouded in mystery. It's known to be capable of stealing life and seems to have a mind of its own, as it occasionally tries to fly away from Abrams (which Abrams can capitalize on, allowing him to cast  Seismic Impact).[16][17] The Tome was also used to conjure Oathkeeper a long time ago.[18] Abrams expresses little control over the Tome,[19][20] and describes it as something "ancient" and "powerful".[21] Knowing that the book is dangerous and can't fall into the wrong hands, Abrams has chosen to participate in the ritual so the Patrons can destroy the Tome.[1][2]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Abrams is stubborn, stoic, and slightly pessimistic. He has a grounded view of the world and is skeptical that the Patrons will follow through with fulfilling his wish.[22][23] That said, Abrams is not unkind, often showing compassion and concern for tragic characters like  Holliday and  Pocket.[24][25]

While stoic, Abrams still gets flustered when talking to  Lash and when  Dynamo teases him about moving into Lady Geist's apartment in *The Binding of Oathkeeper.*[26][27]

Instead of simply dumping the Tome or hiding it somewhere, Abrams feels a personal duty to destroy the Tome to make sure it can't ever fall into the wrong hands.[14] The duty of protecting the Tome has made Abrams paranoid towards anyone who shows interest in it.[28][29]

As a detective, Abrams is often inquisitive of his allies, asking questions about their lives (such as how  Seven survived his execution).[30] Abrams values honesty and the truth, no matter how depressing it can be.[31]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Abrams likes to drink whiskey.[32][33]

Since his car was firebombed, Abrams has been forced to use the bus to get around.[34]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Infernus

[edit | edit source]

As a regular at Jezebel's,[11] Abrams is friends with Infernus and refers to him as "Fern".[35] Abrams also calls Infernus "his bartender".[36]

### Wraith

[edit | edit source]

Abrams plays in Wraith's weekly poker game.[13] Wraith calls Abrams "Abe" and considers him as one of her customers.[37][38]

### Mo & Krill

[edit | edit source]

Mo and Krill are friends with Abrams, and play at Wraith's weekly poker games together.[39]

Abrams owes Mo and Krill $50 from their last card game together.[40]

### Silver

[edit | edit source]

Silver is old friends with Abrams, referring to him as "Abe".[33]

According to Silver, they used to make "bad decisions" before Abrams became "boring".[41]

### Celeste

[edit | edit source]

Abrams is friends with Celeste and her found family. He knows Blockhead Lenny is having troubles and asks Celeste how he's doing.[42]

Abrams seems to be one of the few people outside of Celeste's family who knows she's secretly a unicorn.[43]

### Venator

[edit | edit source]

Abrams has worked on a case with Venator before.

While Abrams' side of the conversation is missing, Venator and Abrams had an incident at a brownstone where Venator made a judgement call that "saved lives", despite Abrams' concerns about Venator's methods. What exactly happened in the brownstone is unclear, but Venator doesn't blame Abrams for "not having the stomach to do what needed to be done", and considers Abrams to be a good man.[9]

### Vyper

[edit | edit source]

Vyper seems to be familiar with Abrams, referring to him as "Abe".[44]

While Vyper comes across as friendly to Abrams, Abrams seems to frequently brush her off.[45][46]

### Paradox

[edit | edit source]

As mentioned in the biography, Abrams has been investigating the Paradox Organisation outside of his case with the Tome.[47]

Paradox threatens Abrams to stop asking questions about them.[48]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- In one of the endings of *The Binding of Oathkeeper*, Abrams moves to  Lady Geist's apartment.[49]
- Abrams is surprised that  Infernus has never visited Ixia.[50]
- Graves' mentor,[51] Lady Geist,[52]  Paradox,[53]  Venator[54] and  Yamato[55] have shown interest in taking the Tome off of Abrams.  Seven is fascinated by the Tome, but isn't interested in taking it.[29]

- Warden wants the Tome to be destroyed.[56]
- Grey Talon says his "stepdaughter" is Ixian, like Abrams.[57] However, it seems that the intended term was "daughter-in-law", as evidenced by Talon's background and Abrams' response.
- Victor asks Abrams for help with uncovering his origins.[58]

## The Binding of Oathkeeper

[edit | edit source]

“This is going to be exciting!”

This page contains game content that is unfinished, work in progress, or unavailable in standard gameplay.

Main article: The Binding of Oathkeeper

Abrams makes an appearance in  Lady Geist's visual novel, *The Binding of Oathkeeper.*

Note: *The Binding of Oathkeeper* is currently inaccessible to the main game, instead being something planned for release in the future. As such, everything in the current visual novel is prone to change, as it is still undergoing development.

### Storyline B

[edit | edit source]

Storyline B - Lady Geist and Abrams successfully summoning the Amber Hand Patron

Abrams plays a significant role in storyline B in *The Binding of Oathkeeper*.

In chapter 3, Abrams visits the gala set up by Lady Geist to find someone who can help her with her failing ward containing Oathkeeper. Abrams gives  Dynamo his business card, asking him to give it to Lady Geist.

In chapter 4, Lady Geist meets Abrams at his office. Abrams shows his Tome to Lady Geist, asking her to place her Oathkeeper hand on a ripped page. After Oathkeeper screams out, Abrams and Lady Geist deduce that the Tome is related to Oathkeeper, now intending to summon the Patrons for answers.

Some time passes as Lady Geist and Abrams succeed in summoning the Patron. Abrams accidentally wastes his wish on asking how Oathkeeper is related to the Tome, only getting told that the Tome was used a long time ago to conjure Oathkeeper. Lady Geist wishes that the missing pages of the Tome be restored, so Oathkeeper would be bound to the Tome instead of her. Now that the Patron has left, Abrams is still stuck with the Tome, now with Oathkeeper inside of it. Lady Geist initially doesn't care about Abrams' fate until Abrams points out that Oathkeeper would come for her if the people after the Tome ever released him. Understanding that her life is still at risk, Lady Geist gets Abrams to move in to her apartment.

Storyline B ends with Lady Geist placing the Tome on a bookshelf in her home, acknowledging that her and Abrams' fates have been intertwined until they can find a way to destroy the Tome.

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

- Abrams originally had a kill line towards  Lady Geist swearing to stop Oathkeeper if it was the last thing he did.[59]

### Neon Prime - Atlas

[edit | edit source]

In Neon Prime, Abrams was originally a character named **Atlas**.

Atlas wore a jetpack and was a time soldier of the Lost Battalion.[60]

## Charge Cancel

[edit | edit source]

Shoulder Charge is  Abrams’ second ability. In it, he charges forward and tackles opponents in his path. During the charge, turning is restricted. Once he hits a wall, it will stun the opponent. You are able to cancel *Shoulder Charge* at any time during the charge.

When you charge forward with no opponents grabbed, your speed is set to 692 u/s (17.6 m/s). With opponents grabbed, speed instantly increases to 1107 u/s (28.1 m/s). Speed does not increase when strafing, unlike normal movement.

When cancelling *Shoulder Charge*, you are able to keep the momentum. When cancelling deliberately for speed and movement, it is called a **Charge Cancel**.

When in the air, you are able to instantaneously change your direction by using *Shoulder Charge* in the desired direction. This can be used to redirect for wall jumps and building traversal.

To maintain the maximum amount of speed from *Shoulder Charge* on the ground, charge, cancel then jump or slide, depending on the situation. In the air, you do not have to input anything afterwards to maintain the momentum.

For a quick burst of speed, jump, *Shoulder Charge* then cancel.

You can cancel at any time during *Shoulder Charge* to maintain the maximum amount of speed; the entire duration of *Shoulder Charge* sets you at a fixed speed that doesn’t change.

Charge Cancelling can be used as a situational escape option when enemies are nearby, or when in combat. Since *Shoulder Charge* starts in the direction you are facing and doesn’t factor in your current velocity, you can Charge Cancel to suddenly change directions.

To execute, use *Shoulder Charge*, cancel, then jump or slide afterwards to maintain speed.

Overview

Update history

Lore

Quotes

Sounds

| Update | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| April 30, 2026 | - Siphon Life heal reduced from 80/40% to 70/35%. - Fixed speed coming out of canceling  Shoulder Charge being too high when hitting a hero. |
| March 21, 2026 | - Melee damage per boon increased by 10%. - Siphon Life range increased from 7.5m to 8m. - Siphon Life T3 range reduced from +3.5m to +3m. - Infernal Resilience T3 increased from +7% Damage Regenerated to +8%. - Seismic Impact impact height increased from 4m to 6m. - Seismic Impact T2 increased from +0.6s Stun Duration to +0.7s. - Seismic Impact T3 Unstoppable duration increased from 4s to 5s. |
| March 6, 2026 | - Bullet damage reduced from 3.86+0.13/boon to 3.6+0.1/boon. - Siphon Life DPS reduced from 29 to 22. - Siphon Life range reduced from 10m to 7.5m. - Siphon Life is now circular rather than just in front of him. - Siphon Life range no longer increases with Spirit Power. - Siphon Life visual range FX fixed to show larger than default radius values. - Siphon Life Lifesteal against heroes increased from 66% to 80%. - Siphon Life Lifesteal against non-heroes increased from 33% to 40%. - Siphon Life DPS spirit scaling increased from 0.5 to 0.6. - Siphon Life T1 increased from -19s to -20s. - Siphon Life T3 now also increases radius by +3.5m. - Siphon Life T3 DPS reduced from 20 to 18. - Shoulder Charge damage reduced from 37 to 30. - Shoulder Charge wall stun duration reduced from 0.6s to 0.3s. - Shoulder Charge spirit scaling reduced from 1.9 to 1.4. - Shoulder Charge T1 changed from "+2.2 Weapon Damage for 8s" to "+40% Slow for 3s". - Shoulder Charge T2 wall stun duration increased from 0.45s to 0.8s. - Shoulder Charge T3 cooldown increased from -18s to -20s. - Shoulder Charge T3 now also grants +1.5 Weapon Damage for 6s. - Infernal Resilience T2 increased from +150 Health to +200. - Infernal Resilience T3 now also grants +20% Debuff Resistance. - Seismic Impact is a little faster to target the location when rising. - Seismic Impact damage increase from 75 to 100. - Seismic Impact now allows you to use items during it. - Seismic Impact radius reduced from 10.5m to 9m. - Seismic Impact T2 changed from "Per Hero Hit: +100 HP and +14% Fire Rate" to "+0.6s Stun Duration". - Seismic Impact T3 now also increases radius by 6m. |
| January 30, 2026 | - Gun Falloff range reduced from 20m-46m to 17m-40m. - Bullet damage growth reduced from +0.154 to +0.13. - Siphon Life T3 reduced from +31 DPS to +20 DPS and Increased Spirit Scaling (+0.12). - Fixed  Shoulder Charge T1 triggering from non-heroes. - Seismic Impact damage increased from 55 to 75. - Seismic Impact stun duration increased from 1.5s to 1.6s. - Improved collision consistency with  Seismic Impact. |
| November 21, 2025 | - Shoulder Charge cooldown reduced from 37s to 33s. - Shoulder Charge T3 reduced from -22s Cooldown to -18s. - Seismic Impact T3 duration increased from 3s to 4s. |
| October 2, 2025 | - Siphon Life damage and spirit scaling reduced by 10% - Siphon Life heal ratio increased by 10% - Shoulder Charge T1 changed from +25% Weapon Power to +20 Bullet Damage Per Shot (results in a weaker followup melee hit) |

**Active Reload** is a Tier 2  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Notable Interactions
- 3 Update history
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- If the player presses the reload button while outside the highlighted section, the item will fail to reload. The item only goes into cooldown once the effect is activated.
- The duration of the Active Reload activation window is always 0.3s. The highlighted section changes size proportionately to the hero's Reload Time.

## Notable Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Vyper benefits from this item to have the smallest downtime to use her ammo sliding synergy.

- McGinnis can use this item to offset her long reload time.

# Air Strafing

| Air Strafing |  |
| --- | --- |
| Air Strafing |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | (Be in the air) → Left/Right (move camera in a smooth motion in the same direction) |

**Air Strafing**[1] is the act of changing direction while in the air using both your movement keys and camera movement. Air Strafing can be used to move around corners, readjust your position in the air and gain a small amount of speed.

The speed at which you Air Strafe in Deadlock changes depending on your velocity; below 450 u/s, air strafing is considerably stronger [2], after which air strafing becomes weaker [3]. Air Strafing in Deadlock is significantly weaker than in other Valve and Source games.

One way of Air Strafing goes as follows: first be in the air. If you are pressing the forward movement key, let go and press either left or right and move your camera in the same direction in a smooth motion.

### Notes

[edit | edit source]

For a more advanced explanation, view Kered13’s steam post on Team Fortress 2’s air strafing. Most of it applies to Deadlock.

1. ↑ Air Strafing is a common mechanic in Source games; if you have played Team Fortress 2 or Counter-Strike Surf, you have probably Air Strafed before.
1. ↑ citadel_aircontrol_speed_slow
1. ↑ citadel_aircontrol_speed_fast

**Alchemical Fire** is a Tier 3  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- With no other items, Alchemical Fire (with its default +8 Spirit Power) deals a total of 384 Spirit Damage.
- Alchemical Fire deals damage instantly on contact, and then every 0.5 seconds thereafter, for a total of 10 damage instances.
- With no duration extenders, Alchemical Fire finishes dealing damage at 4.5 seconds in (the final 0.5 seconds applies the weapon damage effect only).
- Alchemical Fire ramps up its damage gradually, starting at 50% of the max dps at the start, and dealing max dps (100%) from 3.0 seconds and onward.
- With duration extenders, Alchemical Fire will continue dealing damage in further 0.5 sec intervals, e.g. at 5.0 sec, 5.5 sec, 6.0 sec, etc. These damage instances will keep using the max dps values.

# Ammo Scavenger

“Farewell, my friends.”

This page contains game content that has been removed from the game.

| Ammo Scavenger |  |
| --- | --- |
| Cost | **800** |
| Tier | 1 |
| *Passive* |  |
| Any time you secure or deny a Soul from an entity you get ammo back and gain stacking Spirit Power. At Max Stacks, gain bonus Sprint speed |  |
| +2 Ammo Per Soul    +1 Spirit Power Per Soul Conditional    +2m Sprint Speed    45s Duration    18 Max Stacks |  |
| Codename: upgrade_ammo_scavenger |  |

**Ammo Scavenger** was a Tier 1 Spirit Item that provides more Ammo. Securing or denying souls gives you ammo back and you earn one stack of Spirit Power.

It could be purchased from the Shop for  **500**.

Ammo Scavenger's effect of earning back ammo when claiming orbs became a global mechanic when the item was removed, but players earn back 1 ammo instead of 2.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- When a Soul is secured or denied, all stacks of this item's Spirit Power are refreshed for the duration (*30s at base*).
- Also applies when killing Denizens.
- You do not receive stacks when securing spawn room souls.

# Ammo

** Ammo**, also known as **Clip Size**, is a stat that dictates the maximum number of rounds that can be stored and fired from a weapon. As the weapon is fired, the number of available rounds decreases from the maximum to zero, at which point no more rounds can be fired. Weapons can be reloaded to regain rounds up to the maximum.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Ammo under the stamina bar

Ammo is displayed as a number under the stamina bars. The left number is the current ammo count, and the right number is the full magazine capacity.

While sliding, the player has infinite ammo, indicated by a light green infinity symbol.

### Burst fire

[edit | edit source]

For burst fire weapons, each shot fired by the player fires more than one bullet in a short burst. The number of bullets fired per shot consumes the equivalent amount of ammo.

### Alternate fire

[edit | edit source]

For heroes who have an alternate fire, shooting with the alt fire consumes more than one ammo round at once. However, the player can still use alt fire with only one round left.

## Calculation

[edit | edit source]

Ammo is calculated by adding all flat bonuses to your base ammo first, then applying the combined total of all percentage bonuses. Percentage bonuses for ammo are **additive**, meaning they are added together into a single multiplier.

The formula for Clip Size is:

Final Ammo=(Base Ammo+Flat Bonuses)×(1+Total Percentage Bonuses)

**Note:** The final result is always rounded up to the nearest whole number.

### Example

[edit | edit source]

If a hero has **20** Base Ammo and gains the following:

- +10 Flat Ammo from an item.
- +15% Ammo from an item.
- +4% Ammo from a Golden Statue.

The calculation would be:

1. Add the Base and Flat ammo: 20 + 10 = **30**.
1. Add the percentage bonuses together: 15% + 4% = **19%** (or 0.19).
1. Multiply the ammo by the percentage multiplier: 30 × 1.19 = **35.7**.
1. Round up to the nearest whole number: **36**.

### Map spawns

[edit | edit source]

- Golden Statues can provide a permanent increase: +**4%** Ammo before 10 minutes, or +**6%** Ammo before 30 minutes, or +**8%** Ammo after 30 minutes.
- Powerup runes can provide a temporary Gun buff that provides +**35%** to +**70%** Ammo for 160 seconds (scaling with game time from 5 to 40 minutes).

“

Our victory is assured. Unless, of course, the Patron pairs me with a bunch of malcontents who refuse to pull their own weight. In which case, victory depends on how much extra burden I need to bear.

**Apollo** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. With Flawless Advance the fencer begins his approach, timing his strikes perfectly to inflict more damage. Counter-attacks aren't a concern for Apollo, as a flourish of his blade deflects the damage and triggers a quick Riposte, and Disengaging Sigil allows him to jump out of the fray with ease. For his final blow, Apollo dons his fencer's mask and channels Ixia's might with Itani Lo Sahn, leaving enemies defeated in his wake.

As the prince of Ixia, Apollo comes from a land of beauty, tradition and conflict. Political violence was common in Ixia, but when Apollo was sent to New York for his own safety, he knew the situation was serious. Now a highly skilled fencer at Blackmore Academy, Apollo knows that in due time, he will be called back to Ixia... and when he returns, he will show why he's worthy to wield his family's ancestral blade.

Apollo was released on February 12, 2026 as the last hero of the Old Gods, New Blood update.

## Background

“

A land of beauty, tradition and conflict; North Ixia is no stranger to brutal political violence. So when Apollo was told that it was for his own safety he was being sent to New York for school, he knew the situation was serious.

Adjusting to life at Blackmore Academy didn’t come easy to Apollo. His school was supposed to be filled with The Cursed Apple’s best and brightest but all he saw, with few exceptions, was a sea of aggressive mediocrity. Electing not to waste his time with frivolous things like parties and dances, he instead put his energy on the piste, where he rigorously trains as captain of the Blackmore fencing team.

However, at the end of the day Apollo does not fret too much on the tedium of life in New York. He knows that eventually the time will come when his father will call on him to come home and he will get to show that he is worthy of wielding his family's ancestral blade.

A land of beauty, tradition and conflict; North Ixia is no stranger to brutal political violence. So when Apollo was told that it was for his own safety he was being sent to New York for school, he knew the situation was serious.

Adjusting to life at Blackmore Academy didn’t come easy to Apollo. His school was supposed to be filled with The Cursed Apple’s best and brightest but all he saw, with few exceptions, was a sea of aggressive mediocrity. Electing not to waste his time with frivolous things like parties and dances, he instead put his energy on the piste, where he rigorously trains as captain of the Blackmore fencing team.

However, at the end of the day Apollo does not fret too much on the tedium of life in New York. He knows that eventually the time will come when his father will call on him to come home and he will get to show that he is worthy of wielding his family's ancestral blade.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Apollo's wish is unknown, but he seems to be fighting for the sake of Ixia.[1][2] While mentioned that Apollo's father expects great things from him,[3] Apollo claims that he isn't fighting in the ritual for his father.[4]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Apollo is 18 years old[5] and is referred to as "*the Prince of Ixia"*[6] or "*Crown Prince of North Ixia",* though he finds the title inaccurate.[7]

Apollo was taught fencing at a young age, having learned Riposte when he was only 5 years old.[8] He seems to be a fencing champion,[9] and hopes to one day represent Ixia at the Olympics.[10][11] Apollo inherited his sword from his father.[12]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Apollo holds his Ixian culture in very high regard.[13][14] He refers to the other playable Ixians,  Abrams and  Infernus, as his "brothers".[15][16] While he doesn't hate humans, he believes Ixians are above them.[17][18] Apollo is content at Blackmore Academy,[19] but he refuses to see New York as his home and is only there because his father wanted him to be.[20][21]

Apollo is extremely confident in his skills and believes himself to be the best.[22][23] He holds honor and discipline in high regards.[24][25][26] His attitude often causes other characters to regard him as vain.[27][28]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Ixian is Apollo's native language.[29] His ultimate "*Itani Lo Sahn*" is Ixian for "*I have no equal*".[30]

Apollo says his life has been personally affected by political assassinations.[31] Notably, while he speaks often of his father, he never mentions his mother.

The symbol etched in Disengaging Sigil is Apollo's family sigil.[32] He has fond memories of his father teaching him how to cast it.[33]

Apollo has no siblings.[34]

Apollo believes Maximilian Fairfax is a "great man".[35] Both Apollo and his father are fans of Fairfax Industries.[36]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Apollo's father

[edit | edit source]

Apollo's father is referred to as a warlord, and has the authority equivalent to a governor and a general.[37]

Apollo is proud of his father and believes his father is proud of him.[38] His father says "loyalty is everything" and "the first step to victory begins with crushing the enemy's hope".[39][40]

When killing  Silver, Apollo mentions that his father would've turned her into a cloak.[41]

-Graves

-Doorman (?)

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Apollo and  Graves are classmates, and are each other's lab partners.[42]

- Apollo is shocked that  Infernus doesn't speak Ixian nor care for Ixian culture.[43][44]

- Apollo respects  Ivy but believes she shouldn't have saved Spanish Harlem, believing that they should've saved themselves rather than rely solely on Ivy.[45][46]

- Apollo respects  Mirage and  Warden for their conviction and honor.[47][48]

- Apollo sends his father's regards to Ambassador Nashala.[49][50]

- Apollo accidentally invites  Viscous to one of his father's galas.[51]

- Apollo commends  Vindicta for her war against the Friends of Humanity, although he dislikes her dishonorable tactics.[52][53]

- Haze is worried about Apollo participating in the ritual since him dying would cause an international incident.[54][55]

- Krill compares Apollo to a teenage version of  Lash.[56]

- Apollo has stayed at The Baroness hotel,[57] and has tipped  The Doorman.[58]

**Arcane Surge** is a Tier 2  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**. Its component,  Extra Stamina, makes up  **800** of the cost.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Items and passive abilities cannot benefit from the conditional buff - they will not gain additional spirit power, duration, or range.
- The buff which provides the player with the conditional ability range, ability duration, and spirit power lasts for 7 seconds.
- The first ability cast after gaining the buff will consume the buff.
- The conditional ability range and ability duration are snapshot on ability use.
- The conditional spirit power is tied to the 7 second timer of the conditional buff. The +20 spirit power will only be available for 7 seconds after the player initially gains the conditional buff.

Examples:

- 6 seconds after gaining the conditional buff,  Vindicta uses  Assassinate.

- This consumes the buff, and applies +20 spirit power to  Assassinate's damage.
- 6 seconds after gaining the conditional buff,  Seven uses  Lightning Ball.

- The buff is consumed.
- The  Lightning Ball gains +15% ability duration and +12% ability range.
- The  Lightning Ball gains +20 spirit power for 1 second only. For the rest of its duration, it does not benefit from +20 spirit power.
- 6 seconds after gaining the conditional buff,  Seven uses  Power Surge.

- The buff is consumed.
- Power Surge gains +15% ability duration and +12% ability range.
- Power Surge's *damage* benefits from +20 spirit power for 1 second only. For the rest of its duration, the *damage* does not benefit from +20 spirit power.
- Power Surge's total *duration* scales natively with spirit power at time of cast. The additional duration due to the +20 spirit power is snapshot on cast, and is not lost when the 7s conditional buff is consumed.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Armor Piercing Rounds does *not* damage enemies in Invincible state.
- Armor Piercing Rounds bypasses bullet evasion.

## Notable Interactions

# Astral Gates

**Astral Gates** are rifts in space and time connected to the Outer Planes. It is thought that celestial events could awaken them.[1]

Professor  Dynamo is a known authority on Astral Gate research,[2] and he inspired  Seven to do his own research.[3]

## Known Gates

[edit | edit source]

There are 7 known Astral Gates and 1 rumoured, five of these have been mentioned so far.

- **New York** - An Astral Gate was opened in Central Park, which lead to  Dynamo's body being atomised upon investigating it.
- **Atlantic Ocean** - An Astral Gate may have been open in the Bermuda Triangle since as early as the year 565[4] as entities such as the Loch Ness Monster have escaped from the gate. It has also recently released something far more predatory, leading  Viscous to seek out The Patrons in order to keep The Deep safe.
- **Europe** -  A dormant Astral Gate has recently been discovered.[1]
- **Puerto Rico** - The discovery of an Astral Gate led to the annexation of Puerto Rico by the United States.[5]
- **Arctic Circle (Rumoured)** - There is rumoured to be an 8th Astral Gate, a science team assembled by  Kelvin set off to try and discover it. However, the team disappeared and Kelvin was the only body recovered.

At least one of the Astral Gates leads to the plane of Ixia.[6]

# Backdoor Protection

A Walker with backdoor protection active.

**Backdoor Protection** is a type of Damage Resistance applied to Structures when they have no enemy Troopers nearby.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 DPS calculation
- 3 Effects blocked by Backdoor Protection
- 4 Navigation

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Backdoor Protection is indicated by a green circle effect surrounding the structure and the text "Protected" with a green heart icon under its health bar.

Every structure except for Lane Guardians has backdoor protection. Lane Guardians only have protection in the Street Brawl mode.

Backdoor Protection can be removed by pushing the trooper wave up to the structure. For base structures, having any zipline pushed up to the base with no Base Guardians will remove protection. Once protection has been removed, it has a 20s buffer before it's applied again.

Destroying a structure with backdoor protection will instantly push the team's zipline up to the destroyed structure, regardless of it's original progress.

The Backdoor health regen only heals the Structure up to the HP it had before it was attacked under protection. The only structure that can heal up to 100% health out of combat is the Patron, who has 120 HP/s out of combat regen.

| Structure | Damage Resist (%) | Health Regen (HP/s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Walker | 65 | 65 |
| Base Guardian | 65 | 65 |
| Shrine | 65 | 65 |
| Patron | 65 | 75 |

Additionally, Base Guardians and Shrines also have a separate Bullet Resist stat that starts at 40% for Base Guardians and 60% for Shrines, decaying by 20% for each enemy hero nearby, up to 0% minimum.

## DPS calculation

[edit | edit source]

The DPS dealt to a structure with backdoor protection can be calculated as follows:

Final DPS=[Base DPS×(1−Backdoor Resist)×(1−Additional Resists)]−Health Regen

So for example, in a scenario where the player is attacking a backdoor Walker with no additional resists, they need to deal a minimum of 189 DPS (rounded up) to damage it:

1=[188,57×(1−0,65)]−65

## Effects blocked by Backdoor Protection

[edit | edit source]

Certain effects are completely blocked by Backdoor Protection. This is indicated by the "Too Far" damage pop-up.

- Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine
- Venator's  Ira Domini (including the Pure Damage)

# Baroness Hotel

The Baroness, located at Broadway in-game.

“

I think you’ll find the service at The Baroness to be… exemplary.

— The Doorman

**The Baroness Hotel** is a location in the Cursed Apple and the domain of  The Doorman.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Gameplay
- 3 Trivia
- 4 Gallery
- 5 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Baroness Hotel is located on Broadway in the Cursed Apple, as well as being used for  The Doorman's ultimate. The hotel is described by The Doorman as "the finest luxuries this plane can offer"[1], although  Lady Geist believes that the Baroness' standards "went to hell".[2]

The luxuries of the Baroness include bottomless mimosas,[3] an in-house tailor,[4] Egyptian cotton sheets,[5] a sauna,[5] spa days[6] and brunches.[7]

The Doorman has worked at the Baroness since its inception.[8]

Mirage and Nashala are currently guests at the Baroness.[9][10] Carlos and Maria Arroyo planned a date night at the hotel.[11] Ms. Shelly has a brunch scheduled at the Baroness.[12]

The Baroness used to be known as "the most haunted hotel in America", but has lost the title after the Troubadour's actions in Macomb. Now it is only the most haunted hotel in the tri-state area.[13]

At some point, the Baroness required the services of the Baxter Society.[13]

Other known workers of the Baroness are Jacques,[14] and Francis.[15]

## Gameplay

[edit | edit source]

In-game, the Baroness can be found next to the Archmother's blue Guardian. It has two Denizen spawn rooms:

- A room with 3 small denizens.
- A room with 2 medium denizens and a Sinners Sacrifice machine.

The Doorman's ultimate ability Hotel Guest sends an enemy to a supernatural hallway in the Baroness, which they need to escape from.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The Baroness' design is based on the Plaza Hotel in New York.

- There is a real-life Baroness Hotel in Seattle, WA, close to Valve's office in Bellevue.
- Apollo,[16] Calico,[17] Ivy,[18] Krill,[19] Lady Geist,[2] Mirage,[9] and Wraith[20] and  have stayed at the Baroness before. Silver and Vyper have also stayed at the Baroness before, but were kicked out.[21][22] Victor has been invited to the Baroness.[4]
- Paradox is trying, and failing, to gain access to the Baroness.[23]
- There is a brunch going on at the Baroness during the ritual.[7] While inside the Baroness, you can hear distant talking and plates clinking.[24]
- A piano medley can be heard while inside the Baroness.[25]
- The area used for Hotel Guest (The Doorman's ultimate) is located underneath the map.

# Bear Pit

“

You didn't lose money. You spent it learning a valuable lesson: Never bet against The Lash.

— Lash

The **Bear Pit** is an underground arena of blood sport in New York where spectators can bet on prize fights.

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

Known fighters include  Lash and  Bebop, who are rivals. Lash calls himself a "champion" of the Bear Pit.[1]

Lash has lost to Bebop in the Bear Pit once,[2] while Bebop lost to Lash at least once afterwards.[3][4]

Wraith and Krill are prominent gamblers in matches, who are both known to often bet money on Bebop.[2][5] Once, Mendoza told Wraith that Lash was going to "take a dive" in a Bear Pit fight, which Lash proceeded to win, causing Wraith to lose "a lot of money".[6]

Bebop is fighting in the Bear Pit to earn money for Ms. Shelly's medicine.[7][8] He intends to retire once he completes the Ritual and gets his wish.[5]

Celeste's friend Blockhead Lenny once fought in the Bear Pit, but lost to Lash.[9]

Fights in the Bear Pit seem to allow the use of magic.[10]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- In *Neon Prime*, Kali was a former champion of the pit who came out of retirement, only to lose to Bebop. Kali sustained injuries severe enough to send him into an almost 2-decade hiatus afterwards.[11]

“

The inevitable is a hell of a thing.

**Bebop** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. A modified scrap golem with a big heart and a bigger extendable arm, Bebop is a potent threat on the battlefield when supported by his team. His Grappling Arm can pull friends and enemies alike towards him, saving them from certain doom or guaranteeing it. Bebop can attach Sticky Bombs to nearby foes and launch them in any direction with a powerful Exploding Uppercut. For any foes left standing, Bebop's Hyper Beam can cut across the battlefield and finish them off.

The mechanical son of a widowed junkyard attendant, Bebop and Ms. Shelly live together at a junkyard, working with scrap metal by day and listening to jazz music by night. But once Ms. Shelly falls ill, Bebop is forced into illegal activities to pay for her medicine, doing whatever he can to save his creator. While Ms. Shelly wouldn't approve of what Bebop does to pay for her medicine, what she doesn't know can't hurt her.

It also has a short wind-up time to start shooting. The gun can also be wound-up by zooming with right-click.

## Background

[edit | edit source]

*See **Bebop/Lore** for more story content.*

“

Forged by the hands of a widowed junk yard attendant; Bebop was more than just some scrap golem laborer... he was the son she couldn't have.  Together they would work in the iron yard during the day, and listen to jazz at night. It was a predictable, if not comforting routine.  But now, Bebop's creator has fallen ill and while Miss Shelly wouldn't approve of the activities that Bebop does at night to pay for her medicine, what she doesn't know can't hurt her.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Bebop's current model is inherited from his original design in *Neon Prime.* His previous portrait artwork was different from his in-game model and possibly hints at what his final design will be like. This updated design can also be seen in *The Binding of Oathkeeper* Chapter 5D.
- Bebop is voiced by JB Blanc, who is known for voiceworks in many popular videogames (e.g. Diablo in *Diablo III*, Braum in *League of Legends*, Saxton Hale in *Team Fortress 2*, etc.).
- Bebop is named after the jazz style bebop. During Hyper Beam, a saxophone-like instrument can be heard playing erratically, akin to jazz improvisation.[2] The songs Giant Steps by John Coltrane and Bebop by Charlie Parker are possible references for the Hyper Beam SFX variants.
- Bebop has a Cockney accent, commonly spoken in England by working-class Londoners.
- "Ignoring Lash in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Bebop in the Hideout.
- Bebop's Grappling Arm being depicted as a Hook is a reference to Dota 2, where Pudge has a nearly identical ability called Meat Hook.

Forged by the hands of a widowed junk yard attendant; Bebop was more than just some scrap golem laborer... he was the son she couldn't have.  Together they would work in the iron yard during the day, and listen to jazz at night. It was a predictable, if not comforting routine. ## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Bebop's motivation and wish in the ritual is to cure Ms. Shelly of her illness.[1][2]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Bebop describes his creation as "an act of craftsmanship, willpower and sacrifice".[3] Bebop seems to have a soul.[4]

Bebop's main source of income for Ms. Shelly's medicine is by fighting in the Bear Pit.[5][6][7] Once Ms. Shelly is cured of her illness, he intends to retire.[8]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Bebop was created with access to his own free will.[9] While Bebop doesn't particularly value human life,[10][11] he knows Ms. Shelly wouldn't approve of him killing people.[12][13]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Bebop can speak French, but can't speak Japanese.[14][15]

Bebop calls humans "organics".[16][17]

Bebop knows how to bake biscuits.[18]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Shelly Fisher

[edit | edit source]

The creator of Bebop.

Bebop refers to Ms. Shelly as his "mother".[19]

Bebop offers to introduce Ms. Shelly to  Drifter,[20]  Victor[21] and  Viscous.[22] He also wanted  McGinnis to speak to her.[23]

### Lash

[edit | edit source]

Bebop and Lash have a rivalry fueled by hate for each other.[24][25][26]

Lash used to use an uppercut instead of Ground Strike, but refused to use it ever again after seeing Bebop use an uppercut.[27][28]

Bebop has beaten Lash in the Bear Pit once,[29] and Lash has beaten Bebop at least once afterwards.[30][31]

Neither Bebop nor Lash elaborate on why they hate the other so much.[32][33]

Lash has at least 87 reasons why he's better than Bebop.[34]

-Wraith + M&K

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Bebop offers  Pocket a place to stay after the ritual.[35]
- Lady Geist regards Bebop as a man of culture after learning he speaks French.[36]
- Ivy invites Bebop and Ms. Shelly to visit the Arroyo's for dinner.[37]
- Mo & Krill watch Bebop's fights in the Bear Pit and consistently bet on him winning.[38] They know Ms. Shelly and have tried to help her.[39]
- Vyper is a fan of  Lash and dislikes Bebop.[40][41]
- Wraith criticizes Bebop for not telling Ms. Shelly about his work as a pitfighter.[42]
- McGinnis and  Paradox are impressed by the craftsmanship used to create Bebop.[43][44]
- Seven believes Bebop's love for Ms. Shelly makes him weak. Seven threatens that, if he considered Bebop a threat, he would go after Ms. Shelly to get to Bebop.[45]

## The Binding of Oathkeeper

[edit | edit source]

“This is going to be exciting!”

This page contains game content that is unfinished, work in progress, or unavailable in standard gameplay.

Main article: The Binding of Oathkeeper

Bebop makes an appearance in Lady Geist's visual novel, ''The Binding of Oathkeeper.''

Update history

Lore

Quotes

Sounds

| Update | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| April 30, 2026 | - Reduced bullet damage growth by 10%. |
| April 10, 2026 | - Weapon windup time reduced from 0.5s to 0.3s and fast windup time reduced from 0.1s to 0.05s. - Sticky Bomb can now be self cast again, but it deals 20% damage to yourself. - Sticky Bomb radius reduced from 10m to 8m. - Grapple Arm now deals light melee damage (0.7 scaling). |
| March 25, 2026 | - Base health regen increased from 1.5 to 2.5 |
| March 21, 2026 | Street Brawl:    - Hyper Beam duration from -4s to -5s |
| March 6, 2026 | - Hook can now be canceled. |
| February 4, 2026 | - Uppercut T3 heal reduced from 20% Missing Health to 17%. - Sticky Bomb fuse timer increased from 3.0 to 3.5. - Sticky Bomb radius reduced from 12m to 10m. - Sticky Bomb hit/kill spirit scaling reduced from 0.002/0.012 to 0.0015/0.01. |
| February 2, 2026 | - Sticky Bomb on hit/kill spirit scaling reduced from 0.0025/0.015 to 0.002/0.012. - Sticky Bomb T3 duration increased from 3s to 5s. - Sticky Bomb T3 now grants +20% Fire Rate. |
| January 30, 2026 | - Exploding Uppercut T3 no longer grants +100% Ammo - Exploding Uppercut T3 now also restores 20% of your Missing HP on enemy hero hit - Fixed some bugs with  Sticky Bomb tooltip - Sticky Bomb stacks now diminish after 60 hits and 7 kills (rather than 100/10) - Sticky Bomb now drops on the ground and continues counting down when dispelled - Sticky Bomb can no longer be selfcast - Sticky Bomb T2 increased from +70 Damage to +75    Street Brawl:    - Hyperbeam duration reduced from 11s to 7s |
| January 22, 2026 | - **(Undocumented)** Removed the ability to cancel and refund cooldown of  Hyper Beam during casting delay |
| December 30, 2025 | - Stamina regeneration cooldown improved from 6s to 5.5s - Sticky Bomb stacks now count for half for each stack after a certain threshold (100 on hit and 10 on kill) - Sticky Bomb base damage increased from 70 to 80 - Sticky Bomb T2 increased from +60 to +70 |
| December 29, 2025 | - Stamina increased from 2 to 3 - Stamina regeneration cooldown increased from 4.55s to 6s - Bebop Health per boon increased from +46 to +52 - Sticky Bomb base damage reduced from 100 to 75 - Sticky Bomb T2 damage reduced from 63 to 60 - Sticky Bomb Spirit Scaling increased from 1.1 to 1.5 - Sticky Bomb per hero hit from 1.5% to 1% + 0.0025% Spirit Scaling - Sticky Bomb per hero kill from 4% to 2.5% + 0.015% Spirit Scaling |

**Berserker** is a Tier 3  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Gaining new berserker stacks refreshes the duration of all already-existing berserker stacks. It is possible to maintain max stacks by continuing to take damage.
- Stacks are calculated before damage resistance effects such as Bullet Resist and Spirit Resist, but not Invulnerability.
- For example, this means that it is still possible to gain stacks even with Metal Skin active.
- For example, this means that it is NOT possible to gain stacks with Ethereal Shift active.

“

Smash the bottle, smash their heads, smash the ritual!

**Billy** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. A white hot ball of rage, furious at the very notion of... something. Billy is a chaotic front-liner who never backs down from a challenge. With Rising Ram he gets up close and personal, before slamming down with Bashdown to create shockwaves through his enemies. Running isn't even an option when Billy can use his ultimate Chain Gang to grapple enemies and pull them back in. A quick swig from his bottle gets him Blasted, and his enemies totally wrecked.

A furiously livid man with a goat head, Billy kind of believes in a vague idea of something. From looting to public vandalism, Billy makes sure everyone who can be bothered to listen gets to hear "the truth". Don't ask him how he got the goat head.

Billy was released on August 20, 2025 as the second hero of the Six New Heroes update (first winner of hero vote).

## Innate

[edit | edit source]

Billy has a passive that alters his light melee attacks. He can use light melees faster than other heroes (shorter recovery time), gets slowed less when using light melees, and his reload is not interrupted by light melees. This allows Billy to hit the Sinner's Sacrifice jackpot faster than other heroes if he uses only light melee.

Additionally, he can restore ammo when hitting melees once he unlocks his Blasted ability, as detailed below.

- Bashdown procs the melee effects for Blasted.
- In addition to melee attacks against players, melee hits on Structures and Denizens will proc Blasted's effects and extend its duration while active.
- If the player reaches a certain threshold of Blasted stacks by landing multiple melee hits in a short time (10-15s), the Blasted duration will start going down even if the player keeps landing melee hits. However, Blasted can be sustained indefinitely by spacing out melee hits before hitting the max stacks threshold.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- "Billy goat" is a term used for a male goat.
- Billy's weapon name, **Biquette**, means "young female goat" in French. It is a reference to "Biquette the punk rock goat", who went viral on the internet for hanging around punk rock and metal concerts.
- Billy has unused "bespoke" voicelines that make meta references to the game, such as the popular melee Abrams build,[2] calling McGinnis' turrets "aimbots",[3] and calling out Haze for "pressing 4".[4]

- Billy makes a reference to the Rejuvenator rework, saying that "it used to go out to everybody until the Man decided it was too good".[5]
- Billy was one of the heroes in a private build who was accidentally leaked on stream in May 2025. Being early in development, he was using Shiv's model as a placeholder.[6] Billy's work-in-progress portrait was later leaked by an anonymous Discord user in July 2025.
- "Ranting in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Billy in the Hideout.
- One of Billy's in-game hero select screen labels is G.O.A.T., a common acronym standing for "greatest of all time".
- Wrecked was originally called 'Pissed', remnants of this can still be seen while hovering over the icon next to the healthbar while Billy is Blasted.
- Billy had the largest lead in the Six New Heroes contest, at 30%.[7]
- Due to always carrying his bat in his left hand, Billy has a unique reloading animation where he will eat his weapon's magazine before loading a new one that he pulls out from his jacket.

- This animation is also likely a reference to the popular myth that goats can consume and digest any material, including inedible ones.
- Billy possesses a full set of teeth at the front of his mouth. This is unlike real goats, who lack an upper set and instead have a hard dental pad.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Billy's wish is unknown, although the Patrons imply that Billy wants to change the world due to it being "corrupt and beyond saving".[1][2]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Billy got his goat head by using eldritch powers/black magic.[3][4] He implies he turned his head into a goat for a specific reason.[5]

Billy enjoys rioting and looting in New York,[6][7] although he thinks he's the only one allowed to start fires in "his" city (he does accept public rioting if the Knickerbockers win the basketball championship).[8] It's implied Billy uses Shadow Weave to escape the police after committing crimes.[9]

Billy used to use Rising Ram in circle pits before being told to stop.[10]

Billy's mother says Billy's head is "good for nothing".[11]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Billy hates everyone. He especially loathes rich people, such as  Lady Geist.[12][13] He does, however, compliment his allies when they're doing well.[14]

Billy criticizes a Shakespearean Festival, but considers going once  Paige points out that people there would view him as "their king."[15]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Despite being an anarchist, Billy still pays his taxes.[16][17]

Billy believes the Baxter Society never killed real monsters and that it was all a publicity stunt.[18] Billy doesn't believe the Adversary exists until he sees it with his own eyes.[19]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Vyper

[edit | edit source]

Billy and Vyper are familiar with each other. While on the same team, Billy and Vyper flirt with each other. Vyper asks if she can call Billy "Lash", to which Billy doesn't care.[20]

While Vyper holds Billy in high regard,[21][22] Billy thinks Vyper is a moron.[23][24]

It's implied that Vyper knew Billy from before he got his goat head.[25]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Billy thinks  Lash is "chiseled like a Greek God" and has a "sexy mustache".[26]
- Billy believes Carlos Arroyo used  Ivy to increase the property value of Spanish Harlem and to secure his spot as New York's mayor.[27]
- Billy thinks Bebop living in a scrapyard is "kinda cool".[28]
- Lady Geist exclusively refers to Billy as "William". She never calls him Billy.
- The Doorman tells Billy that he's "terribly uninteresting"[29] and "dreadfully boring".[30]
- Bebop calls Billy the "budget version of Lash".[31]
- Vindicta calls Billy out for always talking about the world's problems, but doing nothing to change them.[32]
- Paige wishes she could give Billy a hug.[33] She tries to connect with Billy by seeing past his "mad at the world" schtick, but is unsuccessful.[34]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

In the files, Billy has meta lines when dying to certain abilities, such as "way to press 4, Haze". These lines are unused.[35]

Before his release as "Billy", Billy was referred to in pings as "Furball" and "goat-headed thing".[36][37] These lines were removed in the Six New Heroes update.

# Black Château

**The Black Château** is a mysterious location in *Deadlock*, frequented by academics.

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The Black Château's mysteries were revealed to the general public for the first time in a New York Oracle article.[1]

Dynamo and  Kelvin last saw each other at the Black Château, before Kelvin's disappearance.[2]

Dynamo says "no one is leaving the Black Château" for  Lady Geist's gala event.[3]

1. ↑ Dynamo and Kelvin conversation
1. ↑ *The Binding of Oathkeeper* - Chapter 2A

# Blackmore Academy

Blackmore Academy crest

“

I go to Blackmore. You think money impresses me?

— Graves

**Blackmore Academy** is a school for the children of America's wealthiest families.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Students
- 3 Trivia
- 4 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

**Blackmore Academy** is a high school attended by  Graves and  Apollo.[1][2][3]  Mina and  Pocket are former students.[4][5]

Blackmore Academy is an upper-class school, exclusively for wealthy or exceptionally talented students.[6][7] Krill descibes Blackmore Academy as "the breeding ground for Manhattan's finest narcissists".[8]

Graves and Apollo are each other's lab partners.[9]

Blackmore Academy students seem to have the day off on the day of the ritual.[10]

Blackmore students are implied to frequent Jezebel's, even though they legally can't drink alcohol.[11] Infernus regularly has to kick them out of the bar,[12] which once happened to Mina on her 16th birthday.[13][14]

Some Blackmore students play cards at Wraith's.[15]

## Students

[edit | edit source]

- Apollo - Student
- Graves - Student
- Mina - Former student (graduated)
- Pocket - Former student

**Blood Tribute** is a Tier 3  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Interactions with Crowd-Control
- 3 Update history
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Unlike most active items, **Blood Tribute** has no cooldown or duration limit and instead can be toggled on and off indefinitely.
- The health drain cannot kill its user.

## Interactions with Crowd-Control

[edit | edit source]

- Victor:  Pain Battery (T1 slow.),  Aura of Suffering (T1 slow, T3 extra damage. The effect is negligible.),  Shocking Reanimation
- Vindicta:  Stake,  Crow Familiar
- Viscous:  Puddle Punch,  Goo Ball
- Vyper:  Screwjab Dagger,  Lethal Venom,  Petrifying Bola
- Warden:  Alchemical Flask,  Binding Word (Immobilize Duration. Escape time is not affected.)
- Wraith:  Card Trick,  Telekinesis
- Yamato:  Power Slash (T1 slow.),  Flying Slash,  Crimson Slash

- Arctic Blast
- Crushing Fists
- Cursed Relic
- Knockdown
- Lightning Scroll
- Vortex Web

- Walker - Stomp
- Zipline knockdown stun

The stun induced from a parry cannot be reduced.

This effect helps mitigate crowd-control by shortening stuns' durations, allowing the hero to recover more quickly.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Boho was one of the heroes in a private build who was accidently leaked on stream in May 2025.[1] A playable, although minimalistic, version of Boho was added to the files in the Shop Rework Update. A low quality image of Boho's model was later posted on Reddit in August 2025, and a better quality image was posted on Twitter in December. Boho's ability kit was updated in the Six New Heroes Update, adding three new abilities.
- Boho's codename might refer to Bohemianism, a cultural and social movement related to non-traditional lifestyles of artists during the mid-19th century.
- "Luxuriating in the Hideout" is unused, but is speculated to be displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Boho in the Hideout.
- Boho is referred to as "the witch" by other heroes.

- Billy is the currently the only hero to say "Boho" instead of the witch.[2]

# Boon

Boon counter HUD icon.
Infernus at boon level 1.
Level up notification, rewarding an **Ultimate Unlock** and a **Power Increase**.

**Boons** in *Deadlock* indicate the player's power level over the course of the match. Players gain boons by gathering  **** Souls, which unlocks Ability Points and increases their Weapon Damage, Melee Damage, Health and Spirit Power. The soul count is always visible to all players under their portrait, and the boon level can be seen in the soul container icon next to the player's soul count, and over the player's portrait by pressing Tab. The soul container fills up as the player collects souls, indicating how close they are to the next boon.

The maximum Boon level is 35.

## Contents

- 1 Leveling Up

- 1.1 Reward breakdown
- 2 Ability Points
- 3 Boon Rewards
- 4 Boon Tables

## Leveling Up

[edit | edit source]

**Leveling up** in *Deadlock* is based on a hero's total gathered souls and grants  **Boons**,  **Ability Unlocks** and  **Ability Points**. The first three ability unlocks can only be used on non-ultimate abilities. The ultimate can be unlocked at  **3.6k**.

If the player gathers enough Unsecured Souls to level up but then loses those souls, they will remain at their last unlocked level but lose progress towards the next level equivalent to the dropped souls.

### Reward breakdown

[edit | edit source]

All heroes level up at the same souls-gathered thresholds, in the following pattern:

- Every level-up grants a boon.
- Levels 0, 2, 4 and 6 grant an ability unlock. Every other level grants an ability point (up to 32).

## Ability Points

[edit | edit source]

Ability points are obtained as level up rewards. Each ability has 3 tiers, requiring 1, 2, and then 5 ability points to unlock. It is possible to spend ability points in any order, including saving them to spend on an ultimate ability or for the final level of an ability.

## Boon Rewards

[edit | edit source]

Haze's boon profile. (Image for reference only, numbers may be outdated)

**Boon Rewards** serve to increase the base attributes of the hero. Level ups always grant a Boon Reward.

The base attributes that are improved by Boons are: base bullet damage, base melee damage, spirit power, and base health. Each hero gains unique amounts of base stats from their Boons. The differences in these boon profiles can dictate which heroes are more powerful in the early stages of a game and which heroes become powerful in the late game. Some heroes may have additional stats improved by Boons, such as  Dynamo's bullet resist.

**Boundless Spirit** is a Tier 4  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**. Its component,  Improved Spirit, makes up  **1,600** of the cost.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Currently, it is the only item that gives you a percentage of your current Spirit Power.

## Update history

[edit | edit source]

*View the full update history: **Boundless Spirit/Update history***

| Update | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| March 21, 2026 | - Constant spirit bonus reduced from 35 to 30. |
| July 4, 2025 | - Percentage spirit bonus increased from 13% to 15%. |
| May 27, 2025 | - Spirit % bonus increased from +10% to +13%. |

# Build-Up

Infernus stacking build-up from   Afterburn and  Toxic Bullets on Bebop

**Build-up** is a mechanic that causes bullets or melee attacks to accumulate a status effect over multiple hits.

Whenever a hero fires at an enemy, items and abilities with Build-up add a percentage to a meter on that target. Once the meter reaches 100%, the associated status effect is triggered. The progress of a build-up is shown as round icons above the target. Build-up per shot is reduced by damage falloff, dropping to as low as 10% of its base value at maximum range. For most effects, melee damage also applies build-up.

Build-up is a related but distinct mechanic from Stacks. Unlike stacks, which are discrete increments that scale an ongoing effect, build-up functions as a percentage meter that triggers a single status effect upon reaching 100%.

## Items

[edit | edit source]

Items with Build-up apply their percentage to the target through bullet hits. The build-up meter decays if the enemy does not receive any new stacks for **2 seconds**, at a rate of **20% per second**. Melee attacks count as 1 shot for build-up purposes. Each item's build-up per shot varies by hero, as it is affected by the hero's weapon fire rate and clip size; the exact percentages can be found on each item's page.

| Name | Effect on Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| Slowing Bullets | Movement Slow |
| Weighted Shots | Movement Slow |
| Silencer | Silence |
| Inhibitor | Damage Reduction and Healing Reduction |
| Toxic Bullets | Bleed (Spirit Damage over time) |
| Spiritual Overflow* | Fire Rate, Spirit Power and Spirit Lifesteal |

*  Spiritual Overflow is a special case: its build-up affects the shooter rather than the target. However, the build-up meter still accumulates on the target being shot, meaning it is impossible to accelerate the process by shooting multiple different targets at once. It is also the only build-up source where the progress is not shown above the target.

## Heroes

[edit | edit source]

Some heroes have abilities that use the Build-up mechanic, accumulating a percentage on the target until the associated effect triggers.

- Infernus'  Afterburn: triggers a Burn (Spirit damage over time) effect. Light Melee attacks count as 1 stack; Heavy Melee attacks count as 2 stacks.
- Mina's  Love Bites: triggers a Spirit damage proc. Melee attacks do not contribute to build-up.
- Mirage's  Djinn's Mark: builds up stacks by shooting the target at certain intervals, triggering a Spirit damage proc either when the timer runs out, when max stacks are reached, or when activated by Mirage. Builds up with a single bullet per stack.
- Silver's  Slam Fire (Tier 3): deals bonus Weapon damage if all 3 shots hit the same target.
- Vyper's  Lethal Venom (Tier 3): triggers a Spirit damage proc. Can build up with melee and isn't blocked by  Petrifying Bola.

Note:  Graves'  Essence Theft appears visually as a Build-Up, but it's actually a stacking effect, as the effect is applied over time.

## Counters

[edit | edit source]

Several items and abilities can mitigate or counter build-up effects:

- Plated Armor provides a chance to block bullet effects from incoming shots entirely, which includes any build-up effects.
- Abilities and items that disarm the enemy or reduce their fire rate, such as  Mo & Krill's  Sand Blast,  Disarming Hex and  Juggernaut.
- Dispel Magic removes any existing build-up applied to the player.
- Items providing Debuff Resist reduce the lingering duration of build-up as well as the duration of already triggered effects.

- Debuff Reducer and its upgrades  Spellbreaker and  Unstoppable
- Blood Tribute
- Weighted Shots
- if the player has no build-up,  Counterspell prevents the first shot of build-up. If the player already has a build-up counter, it prevents from triggering when the build-up crosses 100% threshold, but does not prevent the build-up itself.
- Abilities and items that makes the player immune to damage, such as  Ivy's  Stone Form or  Ethereal Shift, will also prevent any build-up on the player.

Notes:

- Metal Skin, despite providing immunity to bullet damage, does not protect against build-up in any way; shots negated by Metal Skin still contribute their full build-up percentage.
- Return Fire does not build up effects against the attacker.

**Bullet Armor** was a Tier 2 Vitality Item that provided Bullet Resist and Weapon Damage to the purchasing hero.

Bullet Armor was a component of Improved Bullet Armor before it was removed. Improved Bullet Armor was renamed to Bullet Resilience.

It was able to be purchased for  **1,250** from the Shop.

# Bullet Evasion

**Bullet Evasion** is a stat that prevents a percentage of incoming bullets from hitting the target. Instead, the bullets will phase through the target, potentially hitting any target behind them.

## Evasion Immunity

[edit | edit source]

Bullets with the following effects cannot be prevented by Evasion.

- Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine
- Mystic Shot
- Lucky Shot
- Armor Piercing Rounds

## Sources of Bullet Evasion

[edit | edit source]

- Grey Talon's  Rain of Arrows T3 gives him 30% Bullet Evasion for the duration of the ability.
- Haze's  Bullet Dance has 30% Bullet Evasion for the duration of the ability, with 40% added on T3.
- Mirage's  Dust Devil gives him 30% Bullet Evasion for 4s after emerging from the tornado, with 30% added on T2.

- This is not a stacking effect, repeated applications will refresh the duration of the debuff.
- The debuff can be utilized by other players. Teammates can benefit from this debuff.
