# Bunnyhopping

Overview

Slide Bunnyhopping

Raw Bunnyhopping

| Bunnyhopping |  |
| --- | --- |
| Load video     Local File     Local File might collect personal data.     Continue Dismiss  https://deadlock.wiki/File:Rawbunnyhop.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Character Dependent: | No |

Bunnyhopping is a movement technique used in video games where the player times jumps immediately upon landing to create a rhythmic hopping motion similar to a rabbit’s movement. The technique originated in early first-person shooters such as the Quake series.

In Deadlock, bunnyhopping exists in two forms:

- Slide Bunnyhopping
- Raw Bunnyhopping

---

# Bunnyhopping/Raw Bunnyhopping

Overview

Slide Bunnyhopping

Raw Bunnyhopping

| Raw Bunnyhopping |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Rawbunnyhop.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Hard |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Stamina: | 0 |
| Inputs: | Jump |

**Raw Bunnyhopping** is a type of bunnyhopping that only utilises jumping.

Raw Bunnyhopping does not consume any stamina.

To execute, jump as you hit the ground, making sure not to air jump. If you do not have stamina, you can buffer jumps by holding space whenever you are about to hit the ground. Raw Bunnyhopping is difficult to execute due to sharing the same input as air jumping.

Raw Bunnyhopping can be beneficial for travelling in a straight line; for moving around corners, Slide Bunnyhopping is better. Perfect Raw Bunnyhops can technically be faster than Slide Bunnyhopping only at speeds lower than 900 u/s, and with good Air Strafing.

To execute, press Jump as soon as you hit the floor.

---

# Bunnyhopping/Slide Bunnyhopping

Overview

Slide Bunnyhopping

Raw Bunnyhopping

| Slide Bunnyhopping |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Slidebhop.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Stamina: | 0 |
| Inputs: | (hold) Slide → Jump |

**Slide Bunnyhopping** is a type of bunnyhopping that utilises sliding. This is the most efficient way for most people to bunnyhop.

Slide Bunnyhopping does not consume any stamina.

Slide Bunnyhopping consists of sliding then jumping; when doing certain actions, a flag can be added to your character that enables **Slide Bunnyhopping**. These actions include;

- Slide Conservation
- Dash Jumping

Any other action will lock you out from jumping during the slide (e.g. Dash Sliding will not allow you to jump). 
When sliding in a Slide Bunnyhop, sliding for *less than 0.5 seconds* at a time will inflict a speed penalty onto you, decreasing speed dramatically. For this reason, it is recommended to slide for more than 0.5 seconds at a time.

The first slide in a Slide Bunnyhop does not have this property applied to it, so instantly jumping for the first one is viable.

To execute a Slide Bunnyhop, first slide. When sliding, jump while holding the slide key. When you touch the ground again, you should slide on the ground again. You can repeat this as long as you have the necessary speed to slide (376 u/s).

**Cadence** is an unreleased Hero in *Deadlock*. She is an Ixian woman and the lead singer of the jazz band **Cadence and the Requiem Boys**.

## Contents

- 2 Weapon

## Abilities

[edit | edit source]

- **Anthem**

Burst into an inspiring song! You and any ally that comes within range get an instant reload with an extra large clip, and have a Fire Rate bonus that increases until the song ends.

- **Silence Contraptions**

Disarm yourself perform a long-range dash melee attack. For the duration of the song, you remain disarmed and your melee abilities apply a debuff that disarms and EMP's enemy targets.

- **Lullaby**

Lull your foes to sleep! Any enemy that comes in range of Cadence sleeps until woken by damage, Cadence goes out of range, or the song ends. Cadence has bonus regeneration while singing.

- **Crescendo**

Encase nearby enemies in glass in an increasing range over a short duration. Cadence then breaks the glass with her powerful voice, breaking any shields on the them, damaging them, and giving them massive bullet vulnerability for a duraiton after.

## Weapon

[edit | edit source]

**Arioso Annihilator**

28 Damage Per Second

Falloff Range

20m  ➞ 58m

Shoots bursts of 4 bullets that embed a crystal shard in the target. After 1 second, the shards shatter and deal the bullet damage again. Shatter damage is doubled if 5 or more shards are embedded.

## Background

[edit | edit source]

### Lore

[edit | edit source]

Cadence is the lead singer of the jazz band *Cadence and the Requiem Boys*. She sings the hit song "Paying the Price".[1] She is a side character in Ivy's visual novel.

Cadence is Ixian.[2]

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Cadence_Song.wavCadence's song "Paying the Price", from Ivy's visual novel

#### Paying the Price lyrics

[edit | edit source]

*The candles are lit*

*They walk in through the door*

*Clad in silken robes*

*The lamb tied on the floor*

*It bleats and it screams*

*Cries that you will ignore*

*The pursuit of power has far worse in store*

*Because you're paying the price*

*There's no turning back now*

*The blood on your hands washes off anyhow*

*We all know that's not true*

*You murdered that girl just cause you wanted to*

## Character interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Ivy works for Cadence in one of her visual novel paths.
- Abrams accidentally calls Cadence "Candice".[3]
- Infernus,  Mo & Krill,  Shiv and  Viscous apologize when killing Cadence.[4][5][6][7]  Wraith says she's her "favorite jazz singer".[8]
- McGinnis is "not a fan" of Cadence.[9]  Holliday tells her to "get a real job".[10]
- Infernus wants to watch Cadence's set after the ritual.[11]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Cadence's model was a modified version of *Neon Prime's* **Sumo** wearing a viking helmet, likely based on the "fat lady" opera singer stereotype.
- Two work-in-progress images of Cadence in Ivy's visual novel, with a new Ixian design, were leaked on a livestream in February 2025.
- Two of Cadence's abilities used music from *Cara Mia Addio*, the "turret opera" song from the end credits of *Portal 2*.
- Cadence's placeholder minimap icon uses an image of the *Neon Prime* version of  Haze
- Cadence and The Requiem Boys are promoted in a theater in the Cursed Apple.

“

I decide when, and where, I strike.

**Calico** is a Hero in *Deadlock*, a former monster hunter turned hired assassin. Possessing her cat, Ava, Calico uses the shadows to her advantage to surprise her foes, slinging Gloom Bombs and attacking with a Leaping Slash for damage and healing. By Returning to the Shadows, she can turn any fight to her advantage, disappearing after a fight or engaging again when the enemy least expects her.

As a contract killer, Calico is glad to finally be earning significant money by assassinating other people. Despite the good that the Baxter Society did by slaying monsters, it simply didn't pay well enough for her.

Calico was added to Hero Labs on October 24, 2024, and officially released on January 17, 2025.

Now an in demand contract killer, Calico is living her best life ending someone else's.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Calico's motivation in the ritual is vague, but she seems to want to be the "Apex Predator" by wishing for power and protection.[1][2]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Calico has been an assassin for at least 5 years, as she was hired to kill  Pocket 5 years before the events of the ritual.[3] Pocket survived the assassination attempt due Calico's bullet missing their heart.[4] It's implied that this failed assassination earned Calico a reputation for "sloppy work" amongst other assassins.[5]

Calico is nicknamed as "the most dangerous woman on the planet".[6][7] She's currently being hunted by the International Police,[8] Scotland Yard,[9] and the OSIC.[10][11] She once assassinated someone named "Siegfried" under  Mirage's nose.[12]

Calico has a son.[13]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Calico is very knowledgeable, knowing things about the Deep,[14][15] the Troubadour,[16] and Oathkeeper.[17] She's implied to know something about  Victor's origins.[18]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Calico learned  Return to Shadows while she was in the Baxter Society.[19]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Ava

[edit | edit source]

Ava is Calico's cat familiar.[20]

Calico adores Ava and refers to herself as "mummy" when talking to Ava.[21][22]

It's implied that Calico makes biscuits for Ava to eat.[23]

### Pocket and Maximilian Fairfax

[edit | edit source]

As mentioned in the biography, Calico was the assassin sent to kill Pocket 5 years before the events of the ritual.[3]

Calico enjoys "tying up loose ends" when she kills Pocket in-game.[24] She also mentions that Maximilian Fairfax will "have questions",[25] lining up with Pocket's belief that Maximilian Fairfax was the one who sent Calico to kill Pocket.

Pocket, naturally, dislikes Calico for almost killing them.[26][27]

### Grey Talon

[edit | edit source]

Calico used to work with Grey Talon in the Baxter Society.

While Grey Talon is disappointed in Calico for becoming an assassin,[28] he doesn't resent her and was content to leave her alone.[29][30][31]

Calico views Grey Talon as a "relic of a bygone era",[32] but also says she will mourn his death if she kills him in-game.[33]

### Venator

[edit | edit source]

Venator knew Calico from when she was in the Baxter Society, but loathes her now that she's an assassin.[34]

Venator believes that, for the right price, Calico would be willing to kill Ava.[35]

When killing Calico, Venator mentions that it was "for Grey Talon".[36] He also references the 30 pieces of silver that Judas received for betraying Jesus when killing Calico, presumably referring to Calico leaving the Baxter Society.[37]

### The Doorman

[edit | edit source]

The Doorman is familiar with Calico and likes her.[38][39] He talks with her about "professional interests in town", likely meaning that Calico told him about her job as an assassin.[40]

The Doorman loves Ava and, in the event that Calico will be unable to take care of Ava anymore, says he'll treat her "like a queen" at the Baroness Hotel.[41][42]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Most characters like Ava,[43] with the main exception of Billy.[44]

- Vyper tries to buy Ava with a "crisp Lincoln" ($5).[45]
- Calico has respect for  Paradox.[46] She also loves the Paradox Museum.[47]
- Calico wants to be friends with  Wraith.[48][49]
- Calico compares Holliday's introverted personality to Grey Talon's.[50]
- Mirage believes Calico is beyond redemption.[51]
- Haze has been ordered to kill Calico. If they're on the same team, Haze says she's going to kill Calico before the day is out.[52]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

Nano (Neon Prime)

When Calico was first added to Hero Labs on October 24, 2024, she originally had a different background:

“

Granted the dubious honor of being named Time Magazine's most dangerous woman on the planet, Calico is an enigmatic occult arms dealer that is willing to fund any and all sides of a conflict if the price is right. 
While her critics (and friends) would correctly identify her as being amoral, she is not without her principles... however cold and calculated those principles may be.

Calico's lore was updated when she officially officially released on January 17, 2025 to her current lore.

### Removed character interactions

[edit | edit source]

Calico has history with Raven and likes him.[53][54]

### Neon Prime - Nano

[edit | edit source]

In *Neon Prime,* Calico was originally a character named **Nano**.

**Capacitor** is a Tier 4  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**. Its component,  Tesla Bullets, makes up  **3,200** of the cost.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Capacitor has an internal cooldown of 0.25 seconds, which is lowered by item cooldown reduction.
- Shock Damage is considered Spirit Damage and is reduced by Spirit Resist.

“

Let's contribute to the chaos!

**Celeste** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. It's not every day that Coney Island's biggest star, The Dazzling Celeste, performs on the streets of Manhattan. Her show begins with Light Eater, where a deep breath lit by her blazing baton coats enemies in front of her, and grants increased damage against them. Following that up, she envelops herself in the prismatic shield of her Dazzling Trick, which explodes and silences nearby enemies who break it. Try not to get distracted by her gliding gracefully through the air, or by the dance of her Radiant Daggers, as you'll regret being underneath them when they rain down from above. As for her memorable final act, the Shining Wonder will make her allies go OOH and her foes go AGGHHH!

A popular attraction at Coney Island, "The dazzling Celeste" isn't a carnie with a horn glued to her head: she's actually a unicorn. As unicorns are nothing more than a myth in the eyes of the public, Celeste hides her true identity out of fear of getting poached for her horn. However, when one of her found family members on the sideshow loses part of their soul in a gambling debt, Celeste is prepared to risk revealing her identity if it means helping her family.

Celeste was released on February 9, 2026 as the fifth winner of the Old Gods, New Blood update contest.

## Weapon

[edit | edit source]

**Carny Life**

Medium Range

Projectile

Bouncy

31 Damage Per Second

Falloff Range

22m  ➞ 60m

Carny Life's projectile flies in an arc and bounces on the first surface it hits. If there's an enemy in range at a narrow angle (~45º) from the shot, the projectile flies in their direction. If shot directly at an enemy, the projectile can ricochet to a second enemy at close distance and aligned at a narrow angle.

Split Shot generates 3 multishots at 70° spread.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Celeste/Lore** for more story content.*

“

Even in a world of magic, some things are still rare and unusual. So what is a unicorn to do?  Announce her presence to the world and potentially have poachers looking to saw off her horn? Or hide in plain sight at a Coney Island Side Show where most folk would assume her appearance was just part of an act?

Over the years "The Dazzling Celeste" has grown into one of the more popular attractions on Coney, and while the applause from a cheering audience is appreciated; what keeps her waking up in the morning is the found family she's made at work.

Keruba the Mermaid.

Blockhead Lenny.

Chickenwing.

Ted.

These were her people.  So when she discovered that one of her own sold part of their soul in order to cover a gambling debt, Celeste knew it was time to step out of the shadows and do whatever it takes to get it back.  Is revealing her power to The Patrons a risk?  Yes.  But that's tomorrow's problem... her family needs help today.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Celeste was named **Pepper** during early development.[1]
- Celeste's appearance alludes to tattooed ladies who worked as sideshow attractions in the 19th and 20th centuries.
- Celeste has unique poses for different directions of her air dash.
- Celeste's Shining Wonder is nearly identical to Lich's Chain Frost ability from *Dota 2* and is similar to the "Skipshot" ability of the unreleased hero Boho.

- There are cut voice lines that indicate Celeste was originally capable of using Dazzling Trick on allies as well as herself, furthering her similarities with Lich.
- Celeste had the most votes from a single player in the Old Gods, New Blood hero contest, at 813.[2]
- Chickenwing and Ted were both teased 3 months before Celeste's backstory was revealed, in a joke post by developer Hopoo.[3]
- "Cleaning Up Glitter in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Celeste in the Hideout.

Even in a world of magic, some things are still rare and unusual. So what is a unicorn to do?  Announce her presence to the world and potentially have poachers looking to saw off her horn? Or hide in plain sight at a Coney Island Side Show where most folk would assume her appearance was just part of an act?

Over the years "The Dazzling Celeste" has grown into one of the more popular attractions on Coney, and while the applause from a cheering audience is appreciated; what keeps her waking up in the morning is the found family she's made at work.

Keruba the Mermaid.

Blockhead Lenny.

Chickenwing.

Ted.

These were her people.  So when she discovered that one of her own sold part of their soul in order to cover a gambling debt, Celeste knew it was time to step out of the shadows and do whatever it takes to get it back.  Is revealing her power to The Patrons a risk?  Yes.  But that's tomorrow's problem... her family needs help today.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Celeste's existence as a unicorn is questioned by skeptics who don't believe unicorns are real.[1][2][3] Some of them believe that she glued a horn to her head.[4] Only her closest friends know her true identity.[5]

Celeste has frequently caused accidents when performing or training her acts.[6][7] She used to close kids' birthday parties with her Light Eater ability until she faced multiple lawsuits.[8] She also took Shining Wonder out of her act after causing too many concussions.[9]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Celeste hates hurting other people, expressing remorse when killing enemies.[10][11] She doesn't like when "the pretty ones" try to kill her.[12]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

The Paradox Organisation have tried to steal Celeste's horn.[13]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Blockhead Lenny

[edit | edit source]

Blockhead Lenny is one of Celeste's found family members.

Celeste dislikes  Lash for beating Lenny in the Bear Pit.[14]

It's implied that Lenny is the friend who sold his soul.[15]

### Mo & Krill

[edit | edit source]

Celeste is close friends with Mo and Krill.[16]

While on opposing teams, Celeste says people like her and Mo were supposed to stick together.[17] Additionally, Mo wants to cry if he kills Celeste.[18]

Krill tells Celeste that she doesn't need to spend her life hiding in a circus.[19]

### Infernus and Hank

[edit | edit source]

Infernus is friends with Celeste and her found family. Celeste invites Infernus to come over to say hi to her family at the sideshow.[20]

Celeste refers to Infernus as "Fern".[21] She's also familiar with Hank and asks Infernus how Hank is holding up.[22]

### Wraith

[edit | edit source]

Wraith has a marker on someone named "Dutch", who seems to be a friend of Celeste as she demands Wraith forgets the marker.[23]

While Celeste isn't fond of Wraith, she does think she's "pretty charming".[24]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Celeste compliments  Calico's voice,[25]  Haze's tie and eyes,[26][27]  Lady Geist's hair and necklace[28][29] and  Mina's dress.[30] She finds Geist "pretty",[12]  Paige "adorable",[31]  Silver a "hot mess",[32] and  Wraith "charming".[24]
- Celeste offers to have a drink with  Silver after the ritual.[33]
- Celeste offers free tickets to  Bebop, Ms. Shelly and  Mirage to see her show.[34][35]
- Celeste "doesn't get the appeal" of  Shiv and says he has "ruined a lot of lives".[36][37]
- Celeste mistakes  Grey Talon's name as "Gary Talon".[38][39]
- Seven thinks it's pathetic that Celeste hides her true power to work at the circus.[40]
- According to  Rem, Celeste smells like peppermint.[41]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

Celeste was named **Pepper** during early development.[42]

# Charge-Up

**Charge-up** is a mechanic that causes items to build up their effects over time.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Whenever you activate an item that has Charge-up, it will activate regardless of whether it finished charging or not. Its effectiveness is based on the percentage it has charged up.

For example, if you activate  Tankbuster when at 50% charge, it will only deal 50% of its damage.

Different items require different amount of times to fully charge up. Charge-Up time is **not** affected by Cooldown Reduction.

| Name | Charge-Up Time (s) |
| --- | --- |
| Mystic Burst | 14 |
| Tankbuster | 14 |
| Quicksilver Reload | 18 |
| Mercurial Magnum | 14 |

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- When recasting  Quicksilver Reload or  Mercurial Magnum, they will refresh their current fire rate bonus regardless of charge-up time, unless the charge is higher then the previous cast, in which case the fire rate is increased accordingly.
- Mercurial Magnum will always give the full Spirit damage on bullet hit bonus, regardless of charge-up.
- Tankbuster triggers on non-player enemies but does not use any of its charge-up.

# Charges

Charges are stored uses of Hero abilities. When an ability with charges is used, a single charge is consumed. When an ability runs out of charges, it cannot be used again until the next charge is ready.

An ability with charges is displayed with a smaller bar above it. The bar's segments represent the number of charges. A white segment represents a usable charge, a purple partially-filled segment represents a charge that is being restored, and a grey segment represents a fully expended charge.

Abilities with charges are still subject to a shorter cooldown between uses. This cooldown varies by ability, and is not affected by cooldown reduction.

## Contents

- 1 Restoring Charges
- 2 Maximum Charges
- 3 Bonus Ability Charges

- 3.1 Sources of Bonus Ability Charges
- 4 Charged Abilities
- 5 Notes

## Restoring Charges

[edit | edit source]

As long as an ability does not have its maximum number of charges, it will passively restore charges over time. An ability's cooldown represents the length of time it takes to restore a single charge.

Charges are restored one at a time, not all at once.

Some abilities do not replenish with time and instead use other condition to gain a charge. For example  Wraith's  Card Trick gains a charge when she deals damage to enemies.

## Maximum Charges

[edit | edit source]

Infernus' catalyst ability upgrades, the first upgrade being to increase the number of charges the ability has.

Abilities with charges can store up to a maximum number of them. Each ability has its own default maximum amount.

Some abilities have upgrades that can increase the number of maximum charges they have. Additionally, specific items can be purchased which grant additional Bonus Ability Charges.

## Bonus Ability Charges

[edit | edit source]

Shiv's Serrated Knives ability with (right) and without (left) Rapid Recharge granting additional Bonus Ability Charges.

Bonus Ability Charges grant abilities with charges additional uses before needing to wait for their cooldown, and are gained from items purchased in the shop.

Bonus ability charges cannot be added to abilities that do not already use charges.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

When the player triggers Cheat Death, a visual effect of a scythe and a contract that reads *"Savor your moments, cheat the end, but remember - Death always collects what is owed"* appears above the player's head.

## Notable Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- The Rejuvenator credit is triggered *after* Cheat Death.
- Victor's  Shocking Reanimation is triggered *before* Cheat Death.

- An exception is for  Shiv's  Killing Blow, which will trigger Shocking Reanimation and Cheat Death at the same time. This is likely unintentional.

# Cheater Frog

Cheater frog portrait
Abrams in the "Cheater's Choice" pop-up

The **Cheater Frog** is an anti-cheat mechanic in *Deadlock*.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

When the game's anti-cheat algorithm identifies a player as a cheater, a pop-up appears to the other players to choose between banning the player immediately or turning them into a frog before banning. The frog is unable to perform any actions besides moving. The match also becomes free to leave and the result is not counted for matchmaking.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The Cheater Frog was based on an unused mechanic designed for *Counter Strike: Global Offensive* that turned cheaters into chickens.[1]
- The Cheater Frog model is the same used in  Pocket's  Affliction. The frog was also originally used for  Sinclair's  Rabbit Hex.

## References

[edit | edit source]

1. ↑ 2024-09-26 - @BurtonJ on X - *"Holy crap, they finally built codename 'FU Surprise Mode'?! When I worked on VAC, Rich and I designed this for CS but the cheater was a chicken."*

# Citadel

“Farewell, my friends.”

This page contains game content that has been removed from the game.

Load video

YouTube

YouTube might collect personal data. Privacy Policy

Continue
Dismiss

*Citadel* early gameplay footage

**Citadel** was an early development version of *Deadlock*. Many of *Deadlock's* game files are still named after *Citadel*.

*Citadel* was reworked into *Neon Prime* at some point between 2019 and 2020.

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The digital book *The Final Hours of Half-Life Alyx* (2020) mentioned "a top-secret new project that another small team at Valve has been working on since the first part of 2018".[1]

References to *Citadel* in other Valve games were first discovered by dataminers in 2019.[2] It was speculated to be a multiplayer team-based shooter set in the *Half-Life* universe, named after the Combine Citadel from *Half-Life 2*. It was also speculated to feature asymmetrical VR-desktop gameplay.[3]

Yoshi shared gameplay footage of an early *Citadel* prototype build that used *Half-Life: Alyx* and *Left 4 Dead 2* assets.[4]

The two teams in *Citadel* initially were named *Team Nick* and *Team Coach,* after the characters from *Left 4 Dead 2*.

# Components

**Components** are smaller items that build into larger, more powerful "parent" items, creating upgrade trees. When you purchase an upgraded item, the shop automatically deducts the cost of any components you already own. This process consumes the component, forcing you to choose which upgrade path to follow.

For example, you can purchase  Extra Spirit for  **800**. From there, you have a choice:

- You can upgrade it into  Improved Spirit for an additional  **800** (total cost  **1600**).
- Alternatively, you could use it to build  Surge of Power for an additional  **2400** (total cost  **3200**).

However, once you upgrade to  Improved Spirit, your  Extra Spirit is consumed. To then purchase  Surge of Power, you would need to pay its full  **3200** price, as you no longer own the required component.

# Console commands

Console commands allow you to modify gameplay settings. If the player has the "Dev command console" option enabled in settings, pressing **F7** will open the developer console, which allows you to run commands. They can be used in the Hideout, Sandbox and "Explore NYC" modes, as well as cheat-enabled custom games.

For a complete list of console commands and variables, see the Valve Developer Wiki.

## Contents

- 1 Useful Console Commands
- 2 All Known Convars/Commands
- 3 Auto execute console commands on startup
- 4 Hosting Custom Games

- 4.1 Adding Bots
- 5 External links

## Useful Console Commands

[edit | edit source]

Commands that require cheats will not work in standard multiplayer matches. To enable cheats in a custom lobby, run sv_cheats true.

| Command | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bot_kick_all |  |  | Kicks all bots from the game. |
| changelevel | See the map command. |  | Loads a new map.   When used in a multiplayer lobby, players will remain connected while the map changes. |
| changeteam | - 0: Select a team and hero. - 1: Join spectators. - 2: Join The Hidden King and select a hero. - 3: Join The Archmother and select a hero. |  | Allows changing your team and hero. |
| citadel_allow_purchasing_anywhere | true/false |  | Enables purchasing anywhere on the map, not just at shops. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_enable_fast_cooldowns |  |  | Enables fast cooldowns, causing all abilities to have a 2 second cooldown. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_disable_fast_cooldowns |  |  | Disables fast cooldowns. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_enable_fast_stamina |  |  | Enables fast stamina, causing stamina to regen very fast. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_disable_fast_stamina |  |  | Disables fast stamina. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_dps_multiplier | number | 1.0 | Adds a multiplier to player damage output. Affects all damage including weapon and ability damage. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_enable_no_hero_death |  |  | Enables invincibility (your health will never go below 1). Requires cheats. |
| citadel_disable_no_hero_death |  |  | Disables invincibility. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_display_new_player_recommendations | true/false | true | Turns the "Great for New Players" banner on/off when selecting a hero. |
| citadel_hero_testing_enabled | true/false | false | Enables the "Testing Tools" menu from the Hero Sandbox. Enabling the menu does not require cheats, but using any of this menu's functionality will. |
| citadel_hero_testing_infinite_money | true/false | false | Gives players infinite souls and ability points. |
| citadel_hud_visible | true/false | true | Shows/hides the HUD. |
| citadel_pause |  |  | Pause the match. |
| citadel_player_move_speed_scale | number | 1.0 | Scales movement speed causing players to move faster or slower. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_pregame_duration | number | 10.0 | Changes the duration of the pregame (countdown before the game starts). |
| citadel_region_override | - -1: Auto - 0: North America - 1: Europe - 2: Asia - 3: South America - 4: Europe (not sure if this is different from 1) - 5: Oceania | -1 | Overrides your matchmaking region. **(Currently does not work)** |
| citadel_show_bullet_lag_compensation | number | 0 | How long to show bullet hitboxes. Green hitbox is client, red hitbox is server. |
| citadel_solo_bot_match | true/false | false | Gets enabled by bot match configs. When disabled, bots don't move. This also enables the pregame countdown.   Not sure what else it does. |
| citadel_create_unit | Hero name from dump_hero_names |  | Spawns an allied dummy bot in front of the player. Requires cheats |
| citadel_spawn_nearby_neutrals |  |  | Respawns nearby neutral camps. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_spawn_practice_bots | true/false | false | Enable to spawn bots when the game starts.   You can also set this to true during a game to spawn bots (although setting it to false, kicking bots, and setting it to true again will not respawn bots). |
| citadel_spawn_practice_bots_count | number |  | Number of practice bots to spawn when citadel_spawn_practice_bots is set to true. |
| citadel_test_survey_popup |  |  | Shows the post-match survey popup asking players to rate the match. |
| citadel_unit_status_use_new | true/false |  | Enables experimental health bars. |
| citadel_unlock_flex_slots |  |  | Unlocks all flex slots. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_unpause_countdown | number | 3 | Changes how many seconds the countdown will last when the game is unpaused. Requires cheats. |
| citadel_weapon_damage_multiplier | number | 1.0 | Adds a multiplier to weapon damage output. Does not affect ability damage. Requires cheats. |
| deadlock_early_development_warning_disabled | true/false | false | Disables the Early Development Build popup when the game starts. This gets set to true if you close the popup after checking "Don't show this again". |
| deadlock_get_old_builds |  |  | Downloads and prints out all of the build data for your account prior to the new builds feature.   Added in Update:August 6, 2024. |
| deadlock_post_match_survey_disabled | true/false | false | Disables the post-match survey. This gets set to true if you submit or skip a survey after checking "Don't show this again". |
| disconnect |  |  | Disconnect from the current match. |
| dump_hero_names |  |  | Lists the internal names of all available heros. Requires cheats. |
| healthpct | 0 - 100 |  | Sets your health to the given percentage of your max health. Requires cheats. |
| hud_damagemeter | true/false | false | Displays your current DPS next to your crosshair. Requires cheats. |
| hurtme |  |  | Deals 10 damage to yourself. Requires cheats. |
| killme |  |  | Kills you. |
| kingme |  |  | Gives you 1.2 million souls and levels up all your abilities. Requires cheats. |
| map | - dl_midtown: The main multiplayer map - dl_streets: 4 lanes map - street_test: Old version of 4 lanes map (before Update:September 26, 2024) - new_player_basics: The Hero Sandbox map - 1v1_test: Seems like an early, smaller version of street_test - hero_testing: Seems like an early Hero Sandbox |  | Starts a game and loads into the chosen map. As opposed to npc_kill, which causes the standard death sequence, this command zaps the NPC out of existence. |
| npc_kill | The name of an NPC to kill (type npc_kill<space> to see a list of names).   If no name is provided, kills the NPC you're looking at. |  | Kills an NPC (troopers, guardians, walkers, etc.).   This causes the standard death sequence with particles, announcer lines, drops souls, etc. |
| private_lobby_create |  |  | Brings up a menu that allows players to create a private lobby hosted on Valve servers.   Added in Update:September 12, 2024. |
| quit |  |  | Closes the game. |
| resetme |  |  | Resets your level, abilities, and souls. Requires cheats. |
| selecthero | Hero name from dump_hero_names |  | Requires you to be on the hero selection screen, or have citadel_hero_testing_enabled set to true. |
| trooper_kill_all |  |  | Kills all non-neutral creeps and guardians that aren't shielded. Requires cheats. |
| trooper_kill_non_bosses |  |  | Kills all non-neutral creeps. Requires cheats. |

## Auto execute console commands on startup

[edit | edit source]

- In the <installation path>\steamapps\common\Deadlock\game\citadel\cfg folder create a text file name it autoexec.cfg
- Put the console commands that you want to run on startup of Deadlock in the autoexec.cfg file, one console command on each line and save it
- In the Steam app right-click Deadlock in your list of games on the Library tab and select Properties...
- In the "LAUNCH OPTIONS" field enter -console -exec autoexec

## Hosting Custom Games

[edit | edit source]

- The host starts a custom game by loading into the map with map dl_midtown

- You may want to pause the game immediately after joining by pressing **P** to give other players time to join the match.
- The host finds their ID by running status

- Find a green line in the console that looks like this: [Client] steamid : [A:1:XXXXXXXXXX:XXXXX] (XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX) (the Xs will be replaced with numbers)
- Select the part after steamid that looks like this, including the square brackets: [A:1:XXXXXXXXXX:XXXXX]
- Right click and choose "Copy Selected Text"
- The host sends players the ID they just copied. Players can now connect to the game by opening their console and running connect [A:1:XXXXXXXXXX:XXXXX] (replace the part after connect with the ID they got from the host).
- Upon joining, players will be able to select their team and hero. To bring up this menu again, players can run changeteam 0.
- If you ever want to restart the game, the host can run changelevel dl_midtown .

### Adding Bots

[edit | edit source]

- On the main menu, before you start the game, run exec citadel_botmatch_practice_6v6 to load the bot config.

- If you're already in a game, you can perform these steps then run changelevel dl_midtown to restart the game instead of starting a new one.
- Run citadel_spawn_practice_bots false so that bots won't spawn immediately when the game starts.
- Run citadel_spawn_practice_bots_count 12 to ensure that bots fill all remaining slots (they'll be added until both teams have 6 players).
- Start the game (i.e. map street_test) and press **P** to pause the game during the pregame (as soon as you load in).

- You can use citadel_pregame_duration before starting the game to increase the duration of the pregame if you want.
- Allow all other human players to connect and select their team and hero.

- The team/hero menu can be a bit glitchy. Players can use the changeteam command instead (see table above for command description).
- Remember to choose your (the host's) own team and hero as well. This may automatically unpause the game - press **P** after selecting a team to pause again.
- After all human players have joined teams and selected heroes, the host runs citadel_spawn_practice_bots true, then presses **P** again to unpause the game. Bots should fill the remaining slots on each team.

# Cosmic Veil

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Veil_Greyside.mp4The Grey side of a Cosmic Veil. Heroes and their Minions are obscured on the other side.
https://deadlock.wiki/File:Veil_Rainbowside.mp4The Rainbow side of a Cosmic Veil. Heroes and their Minions are visible on the other side.

**Cosmic Veils** are visual barriers located around the Map at all Juke Rooms and beneath most structural arches. They do not block movement, but slightly obscure vision beyond the barrier acting like one-way window film. Depending on the side, the barrier will either be of a gray colorless filter or rainbow shine filter.

On the gray colorless side, it will block out any perception of color and more importantly hide all enemy heroes as well as abilities performed by any player from the opposite side. Several visual effects will be visible but most player created game objects cannot be seen through the gray side.

Meanwhile, the rainbow shine side will allow players to see others on the other side of the cosmic veil. As such, this game mechanic is often used as a means in positioning to attack enemies with surprise or escaping from a chase.

## Notable Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- An item that takes advantage of the abundance of these cosmic veils while providing additional benefits from their usage is the Tier 3 Vitality Item,  Veil Walker, which can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**.
- The grey side of the veil breaks line of sight for abilities like  Billy's  Chain Gang,  Lash's  Death Slam and  McGinnis'  Mini Turrets. The rainbow side of the veil breaks line of sight for Death Slam but not for other abilities.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The rainbow shine side of a cosmic veil is based on a real world natural phenomenon called thin-film interference, where white light is split into different wavelengths creating a rainbow pattern on a thin-film formed on soap, oil, types of protective coating, etc.

**Counterspell** is a Tier 3  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Notable interactions
- 3 Update history
- 4 Gallery
- 5 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Counterspell is visually indicated by a purple bubble VFX replacing the default parry effect.
- Counterspell only goes on cooldown on a successful spell parry.
- The player can parry multiple abilities during the Counterspell parry window. The heal and buffs are only applied for the first parry.
- Like regular parries, Counterspell has a short grace period where the parry procs after the parry animation has finished.

## Notable interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Counterspell prevents all damage from a Walker stomp and Shrine defense, but does not prevent the stun and knockback. It also does not prevent the Shrine's Curse status effect.
- Counterspell prevents all damage and Curse effect from the Patron's defensive attack.
- Counterspell does not proc when parrying  Viscous'  Puddle Punch, since the ability can be blocked by regular parries.
- Counterspell can prevent  Lash's  Death Slam if the player parries at the moment they would be pulled.
- Counterspell can be used on  The Doorman's  Hotel Guest.
- Counterspell can be used on  Celeste's  Shining Wonder. However, the orb will continue to linger on the player and can bounce onto other heroes.
- Counterspell can prevent Build-Up effects such as  Mina's  Love Bites and stacking effects such as  Haze's  Fixation, if activated either before the build-up is applied or when it triggers. If build-up/stacks have already been applied, it does not prevent the build-up itself.
- Counterspell can prevent  Mirage's  Djinn's Mark before it's applied to the player. However, it does not prevent it from stacking or triggering once it has been applied.
- Counterspell can block instant abilities such as  Mo & Krill's  Combo if the enemy tries to use the ability during the target's parry window, similarly to  Unstoppable.

# Crates

Crates

Crates (or boxes) are breakable objects scattered around the map that, when broken, have a chance to drop Unsecured Souls. Crates can be broken by shooting, punching, using certain abilities, dashing, or sliding through them.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Soul Values
- 3 Notes
- 4 Update history
- 5 Lore
- 6 Trivia
- 7 Gallery

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Crates spawn after 2 in-game minutes (with the exception of a large group of breakables placed in the room directly above the Mid-Boss pit, which instead spawn after 10 in-game minutes), and respawn 3 minutes after being broken. Souls provided from crates are Unsecured Souls. Not collecting the souls and leaving them on the ground will delay the respawn if they aren't collected within the normal respawn time.

Souls collected from crates are tracked in the post-game "Souls by Source" graph as "Breakable Pickups".

## Soul Values

[edit | edit source]

- **Value:** Soul Value of the target at the very beginning of a match
- **Gain:** How the soul value changes over the time of the match, measured in minutes
- **2 min:** Value of the target at the initial moment of spawn
- **10 min/20 min/30 min:** Value of the target at certain game times

| Source | Chance | Value | Gain (/min) | 2 min | 10 min | 20 min | 30 min | 40 min | 50 min | 60 min |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Crates | 60% | 23 | 2.0 | 27 | 43 | 63 | 83 | 103 | 123 | 143 |

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Even though crates spawn after 2 in-game minutes, their soul scaling starts immediately.

# Crouch Gliding

| Crouch Gliding |  |
| --- | --- |
| Load 動画     Local File     Local Fileは個人データを収集する可能性があります。     コンティニュー 非表示  https://deadlock.wiki/File:Crouchgliding.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | (Move ≥ 10 m/s or 376 u/s) → Slide → ShootM1 → Release Slide → Stop shootingRelease M1 → Repeat from Slide |

Sliding is available when you are moving at speeds higher than 10 m/s or 376 u/s. By buying items that increase move or sprint speed, you can attain movement speeds above that threshold.

Moving at speeds higher than *10* m/s or *376* u/s and then sliding repeatedly is called a **Crouch Glide**. By pressing the duck key repeatedly, you initiate a slide for short periods of time. This can make you (and your head hitbox) harder to hit due to the constant movement of your character.

Timing the crouch key correctly is essential, since aggressive crouch spamming causes you to move slower; try to prolong the slide instead of blindly spamming the duck key.

While you are sliding, you have infinite ammo. If you shoot while sliding, you can conserve ammunition. However, this can be hard to properly time; you have to repeatedly press and let go of the fire button every time you slide to prevent M1 Lockout (summary: you cannot hold M1).

To execute Crouch Gliding, have a move speed of above *10* m/s or *376* u/s. While moving above the speed threshold, repeatedly press crouch. If you want to shoot during a Crouch Glide, press M1 during the slide.

# Crouching

| Crouching |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Crouching.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Basic Mechanics |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Press the duck keyBy default, CTRL |

Crouching is a basic action available to the whole cast.

When crouching, you’ll nearly instantly decelerate to 4.8 m/s, stopping momentum. This can be used for more efficient direction changes while moving (tap crouch and change direction).

When moving over 8.9 m/s or 350 u/s, you will instead slide.

# Crowd Control

*See also Status Effects for a comprehensive list of all sources of Crowd Control and other Status Effects.*

“

All they'll be able to do is stand there and burn.

— Venator

**Crowd Control (CC)** refers to effects that alter an opponent's capability to function, including their movement, ability use, weapon firing, and many others. Applying a CC effect to an enemy is reduced in duration when affected by other CC effects within the last 9 seconds. This duration reduction starts at 15% and scales to 35%.

They can be applied both by Hero abilities and Items from the Shop.

## Contents

- 1 Types of Crowd Control

- 1.1 Movement Slow
- 1.2 Stun
- 1.3 Sleep
- 1.4 Immobilize
- 1.5 Silence
- 1.6 Item Silence
- 1.7 Disarm
- 1.8 Interrupt
- 1.9 Displace
- 1.10 Time Stop
- 1.11 Hex
- 2 Crowd Control Reductions and Immunities

- 2.1 Slow Resistance
- 2.2 Invincibility
- 2.3 Purge
- 2.4 Unstoppable

## Types of Crowd Control

[edit | edit source]

### Movement Slow

[edit | edit source]

Reduces the target's movement speed by a percentage.

For example, a 30% slow reduces a 10 meters / second movement speed to 7 m/s.

Movement Slow cannot reduce a target's speed below 2 meters / second.

### Stun

[edit | edit source]

Prevents the target from shooting, using abilities, using items, and moving. Stun also causes the target to be Interrupted.

Examples include  Infernus'  Concussive Combustion,  Ivy's  Stone Form, and  Dynamo's  Singularity.

### Sleep

[edit | edit source]

Similar to Stun, it prevents the target from shooting and using abilities. However, unlike Stun, it **does not** prevent movement; instead, it slows the target to 2m/s.

Sleep does not Interrupt channels. Receiving any damage wakes the target instantly.

Sources of Sleep include abilities such as  Haze's  Sleep Dagger and  Rem's  Naptime.

### Immobilize

[edit | edit source]

Reduces all speed to 0 and stops all voluntary movement, though the target can still be displaced by others. Additionally, it prevents the use of movement related abilities. It removes all upwards acceleration, making airborne targets fall to the ground.

Examples include  Warden's  Binding Word,  Paige's  Captivating Read, and  Arctic Blast.

### Silence

[edit | edit source]

Prevents the target from activating abilities, though they can still use Item actives.

A common cause of confusion is that  **Silence** does not Interrupt, meaning abilities that have started will always continue through Silence, such as  Seven's  Storm Cloud.

Examples include  Silence Wave,  Silencer,  Focus Lens,  Wraith's  Telekinesis, and more.

### Item Silence

[edit | edit source]

Prevents the target from using Item actives, though they can still use abilities.

Examples include  Cursed Relic (disables all items) and  Slowing Hex (disables movement items).

### Disarm

[edit | edit source]

Prevents the target from firing their main weapon but melee attacks can still be used. Note that abilities that use weapon-damage can still be used while  **Disarmed**, such as  Haze's  Bullet Dance.

Examples include  Mo & Krill's  Sand Blast and  Disarming Hex.

### Interrupt

[edit | edit source]

Interrupts instantly cancel all ability casts and channels. It alone does not prevent further use of abilities. When targets are Stunned they are also Interrupted.

Examples of Interrupt (other than Stun) include the  Cursed Relic and  Knockdown Items and  Grey Talon's  Spirit Snare.

### Displace

[edit | edit source]

Exerts some force on the target that modifies their acceleration or velocity, moving or knocking them around.

Examples include  Lash's  Ground Strike,  Bebop's  Exploding Uppercut and  Grapple Arm,  Vindicta's  Stake, the  Rescue Beam and  Knockdown Items, and more.

### Time Stop

[edit | edit source]

The target acts as if time is frozen or slowed, slowing their movement, animations, casts, channels.

The effects of time stopped abilities can still function. For example, if  Dynamo is time stopped during his  Singularity channel, it still pulls and stuns enemies. Note that this technically lengthens the duration of the  Singularity.

Examples include  Apollo's  Itani Lo Sahn,  Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine, and  The Doorman's  Hotel Guest.

### Hex

[edit | edit source]

The target is transformed into a rabbit.

The target gains a smaller model and hitbox and moves faster, but will take increased damage. Hexed targets cannot use their weapon, melee, abilities, or items. Abilities and heavy melee attacks will not be interrupted when hexed.

The only source of Hex is  Sinclair's  Rabbit Hex.

## Crowd Control Reductions and Immunities

[edit | edit source]

Effects that reduce the intensity of crowd control, either partially or completely.

### Slow Resistance

[edit | edit source]

Reduce the effectiveness of slows.

𝑀𝑜𝑑𝑖𝑓𝑖𝑒𝑑𝑆𝑝𝑒𝑒𝑑=𝐵𝑎𝑠𝑒𝑆𝑝𝑒𝑒𝑑*(1−𝑆𝑙𝑜𝑤*(1−𝑆𝑙𝑜𝑤𝑅𝑒𝑠𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒))

For example,  Infernus'  Flame Dash normally moves at 12 meters per second, but with a 30% slow and its innate 50% slow resistance it is slowed down by 15% to 10.2m/s.

### Invincibility

[edit | edit source]

Become unable to be hit or targeted. All projectiles and area effects phase through while you also can not be targeted by Items such as  Cursed Relic or Abilities such as  Mo & Krill's  Combo.

Examples include  Ethereal Shift and  Calico's  Return to Shadows and the transformation phase of  Yamato's  Shadow Transformation.

While  Yamato cannot move during the transformation phase, both  Ethereal Shift and  Return to Shadows allow limited movement.

### Purge

[edit | edit source]

Instantly remove all debuffs.

Some debuffs delay the crucial negative effect, such as  Mirage's  Djinn's Mark. Therefore, if the mark is applied, then the target purges their debuffs, the mark never detonates.

Examples include  Viscous'  The Cube (Tier 3),  Yamato's  Shadow Transformation, and  Dispel Magic.

### Unstoppable

[edit | edit source]

Become immune to all forms of crowd control.

For example the  Unstoppable Item,  Abrams'  Seismic Impact (Tier 3), and  Yamato's  Shadow Transformation.

**Cultist Sacrifice** is a Tier 3  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**. Its component,  Monster Rounds, makes up  **800** of the cost.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Using Cultist Sacrifice on an NPC gives the player the full soul bounty plus 170% (270% total). The original bounty and the bonus are displayed as two separate values when activated.
- The buff persists through death.
- Cultist Sacrifice applies additional damage to Non-Player Characters. This includes Troopers, lane structures like Guardians, Walkers, neutral entities such as Denizens, and the Patron.
- It does apply additional damage against  Graves'  Ghouls, but *not* against  McGinnis'  Mini Turrets. However, both of them can be consumed for the buff and bonus souls.
- Cultist Sacrifice's active counts as Spirit Damage. This means it can activate on-hit spirit damage procs such as  Spirit Burn.
- When Cultist Sacrifice comes off cooldown, a whispering voice can be heard demanding a sacrifice.

# Damage Barrier

“Cannot waste time.”

This page is outdated and it needs to be updated. You can help the Deadlock Wiki by updating it.

**Notes:** The list of hero abilities is a bit outdated after the March 6 2026 update

Pocket with 600 HP barrier

**Barriers** are a temporary pool of additional health that takes damage before Health is reduced. Barriers block all incoming damage from any source, with Damage Resistances applied.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Any instance of excess damage dealt to completely destroy a barrier is then done to health.

- For example, a Dynamo with 100 barrier health and 0% Spirit Resist takes 168 spirit damage from Vindicta's Assassinate. 100 spirit damage will break Dynamo's barrier, the remaining 68 spirit damage is done to health.

# Damage Resistance

**Damage Resistance** refers to the Bullet, Melee, and Spirit Resist statistics which reduce incoming damage taken. Bullet Resist reduces all weapon and melee damage, Melee Resist reduces only melee damage, while Spirit Resist reduces all spirit damage. Units have a unique "Damage Resistance" stat that is applied to all sources of damage, including Troopers.

Most resistances stack multiplicatively; they are not added together. Sources of Resistance Reduction are multiplied together separately first. The total reduction is then subtracted from the total resistance. This has the consequence of resistance reduction being more effective on targets with higher resistance.

## Resistance types

[edit | edit source]

In addition to the basic types of Bullet and Spirit Resistance, there is also Melee Resist and Crit Reduction.

### Melee Resist

[edit | edit source]

Melee Resist is a stat that reduces all incoming melee damage, including from melee abilities such as  Viscous'  Puddle Punch. It increases equally to Bullet Resist (e.g. an item that gives 10% Bullet Resist also gives 10% Melee Resist). Some items also give bonus Melee Resist. Like other types of resist, it stacks multiplicatively.

### Crit Reduction

[edit | edit source]

Crit Reduction is a stat that reduces the critical damage (headshots) received by the hero. Not to be confused with Crit Bonus Scale, a stat that reduces the critical damage dealt by the hero to other targets.

## Calculation

[edit | edit source]

While items often display resistance as a flat percentage (e.g., +20% Resist), multiple sources of resistance do not simply add together. Instead, they stack **multiplicatively**.

### Calculating Resistance

[edit | edit source]

To find your total resistance, use the following formula:

Total Resist=1−(1−R1)×(1−R2)…

**Example:**
If you have two sources of resistance, one providing **40%** and another providing **20%**:

1. Convert percentages to decimals: 0.40 and 0.20.
1. Subtract from 1: (1 - 0.40) = **0.60** and (1 - 0.20) = **0.80**.
1. Multiply the remainders: 0.60 × 0.80 = **0.48**.
1. Subtract from 1: 1 - 0.48 = **0.52**.
1. Your Total Resist is **52%**.

### Calculating Resistance Reduction

[edit | edit source]

**Resistance Reduction** (often called "shred") acts as a counter to resistance. It is calculated separately using the same multiplicative formula, and then subtracted from the target's resistance.

Final Resist=Total Resistance−Total Reduction

**Example:**
A target has **52%** Total Resistance (as calculated above). You attack them with two sources of Reduction: one providing **25%** and another providing **20%**.

**Step 1: Calculate Total Reduction**
1−(1−0.25)×(1−0.20)=0.40→𝟒𝟎%

**Step 2: Subtract Reduction from Resistance**
52%−40%=𝟏𝟐%

The target has a final effective Resist of only **12%**.

### Negative Resistance

[edit | edit source]

If the Total Reduction is higher than the Total Resistance, the final value will be negative. This acts as a damage amplifier.

- **30% Resist:** You take **70%** of incoming damage.
- **0% Resist:** You take **100%** of incoming damage (True Damage).
- **-30% Resist:** You take **130%** of incoming damage.

# Damage per second

Damage per second, or **DPS**, is a function of a hero's Bullet Damage and Fire Rate. It refers to the amount of damage per second the hero's weapons will deal if continuously fired, and is calcuated by the amount of bullets shot per second multiplied by the bullet damage.

| Dashing |  |

| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Basic Mechanics |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | DashBy default, the left shift key |

**Dashing** is a fundamental part of movement in Deadlock. Dashing allows you to quickly evade attacks, to reposition fast and efficiently, and is a basic building block for other basic and advanced movement techniques.

Dashing takes one bar of stamina. You can dash both in the air and on the ground; when done in the air, it is called an **Air Dash**. You are only permitted one Air Dash per jump at the start of the game; this can be expanded to two with the  Vitality Item  Stamina Mastery.

Using a keyboard, you can dash in four directions on the ground (the four cardinal directions) and nine in the air (the eight inter-cardinal directions plus directly down). If you are using a joystick to move, you can dash at any angle on the ground and in the air.

While in the air, you have access to one other direction to dash to; down towards the ground. When you dash towards the ground, it is called a **Down dash**. To down dash, double tap the duck key; once you press the duck key, you have a *28 ticks* (*0.44* second) window to press it again.[1]

Dash choices on the ground.

*0.3* seconds after starting a grounded dash, a window to execute a Dash Jump will open for *0.2* seconds,[2] during which the stamina bar flashes a light blue. This window is solely activated by starting a grounded dash; if you leave the ground after initiating the dash, you are still able to dash. For more information, view the dedicated page on Dash Jumping.

While everyone in the roster has the same dash distance, they have different dash speeds. Characters fall into three **buckets**[3]:

- **Bucket 1** characters have the fastest dash speed, with peak speeds of *635* u/s on the ground and a total dash time of *0.62* seconds.[4]
- **Bucket 2** characters have 9% slower dash speed, with peak speeds of *579* u/s on the ground and a total dash time of *0.68* seconds.[5]
- **Bucket 3** characters have the slowest dash speed, being 12% slower than Bucket 1, with peak speeds of *562* u/s on the ground and a total dash time of *0.70* seconds.[6]

Dashing on the ground always sets your velocity to a fixed amount. Air Dashing is an *impulse* instead, meaning it can stack or conflict with prior momentum.

Dash choices in the air.

To dash, move and press the dash keyBy default, the left shift key. Your character will quickly move in that direction.

| Character Dependent: | YesOnly characters who currently have AnimGraph 2 enabled |
| Stamina: | 0 |

AnimGraph2 is a new, more optimised animation system implemented in certain Source 2 games. AnimGraph2 is intended to replace the older, less optimised AnimGraph system.

During the switch to AnimGraph2, certain animations have had their properties changed, resulting in strange or unusual interactions compared to the rest of the cast. As of current writing, all characters have switched over to AnimGraph2.

**Ag2Dashing** only works during set times in the match and is dash bucket dependent.  The times listed below are until the hour; there may be additional time windows after.

| Bucket | 1st Time Window | 2nd Time Window | 3rd Time Window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bucket 1 | 0:00–0:15 | 0:30–1:01 | 2:05–34:03 |
| Bucket 2 | 0:00–0:05 | 2:05–17:01 | 34:03 onwards |
| Bucket 3 | 0:00–0:15 | 1:19–4:12 | 17:03 onwards |

By dashing and then crouching on a ramp on the next tick, you can gain a large impulse of speed, with peaks of 1065 u/s. This speed quickly tapers off due to sliding friction.

During the laning phase, this can be a faster way of reaching troopers to deny or confirm them. Outside of the laning phase, this technique is extremely niche.

# Dashing/Dash Jumping

| Dash Jump |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Dashjumping.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Basic Mechanics |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Dash → Jump (when timing window is open) |

**Dash Jumping** is a quintessential part of high level and advanced movement in Deadlock. Dash Jumping costs two bars of stamina.

While dashing, a small timing window opens (the window is open for 0.2 seconds, which starts 0.3 seconds into the dash) for the execution of a dash jump, during which the stamina bar quarter-circle will flash blue. If done correctly, your character will execute a dash jump. If you fail the timing, you will be locked out of the dash jump.

Dash Jumps work by setting your velocity to a fixed sequence; prior momentum is disregarded and your speed is instantly set to 611 u/s. For this reason, Dash Jumps are not recommended for continuing momentum and in the middle of movement sequences with techniques such as ZMCZipline Momentum Conservation. Because speed is set to a fixed amount which is relatively high compared to normal walking and sprinting speeds, Dash Jumps are usually used at the start of movement sequences for a quick burst of momentum.

If you leave a ledge after the initial dash, the Dash Jump window will still be open; this means that you can Dash Jump in the air if the initial dash was grounded. Intentionally doing this is called a **Coyote Dash Jump**. This is very useful if you are trying to maximise the distance covered. This Dash Jump will not count as an air action, meaning you preserve your Air Jumps and Wall Jumps.

[edit | edit source]

**Dash Jump Slide BunnyhopName by LȊGHTBRINGER** lets you maintain momentum after a Dash Jump. Immediately after Dash Jumping, you are airborne; by holding the crouch key, you can initiate a slide upon landing. While sliding, perform a bunnyhop to preserve speed and move faster across the map for the same stamina cost.

This does not consume extra stamina, making it useful for navigating the map or chasing opponents in non-linear paths. To execute, perform a Dash Jump, then strafe in midair while moving to redirect your trajectory.

# Dashing/Dash Sliding

Overview

Strafe Dashing

Dash Jumping

Ag2 Dashing

| Dash Sliding |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Dashsliding.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Dash then hold crouch to slide |

Ground dashes are eligible to be cancelled into a slide at any time. When this is performed, it is called a **Dash Slide**.

Dash Sliding costs one bar of stamina.

Dash Sliding is useful for multiple reasons. It:

- Allows you to maintain some speed out of a regular dash (since a regular dash ends at regular walking speed) and allows you to travel more distance in comparison to a regular dash.
- Puts you into the slide state, which is useful for combat and doesn't lock you out of shooting.
- Only consumes one bar of stamina, which can be preferable to a Dash Jump.
- Is easily cancellable, unlike regular dashes which can only be cancelled by a slide.

Dash Sliding for the full duration is not advisable; sliding for the full duration will cause you to eventually move at a speed slower than walking; instead, cancel the slide roughly when the Dash Jump circle turns blue.

| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |

**Instant Air DashingAlso known as *IAD*** is the act of jumping then instantly air dashing. This removes the slowdown that happens at the end of each regular dash.

IAD's only costs one bar of stamina.

Without items, an IAD is slower than a regular dash, air dash and Dash Jumping. However, with the  Vitality Item  Stamina Mastery, and combined with Slide Bunnyhopping, IAD's becomes significantly faster and travels further.

Dashing once gives a substantial amount of speed and distance for one bar; a good IAD with slide bunnyhopping can give the distance of a dash jump with half the stamina cost. Air Dashing twice increases the peak speed from the speed of a regular dash to ~900 u/s and the distance to around two dash jumps.

IAD’s also can give a small amount of momentum to abilities if timed correctly.

**Short Dash Crouch CancellingAlso known as SDCC, Dash Cancelling. Name by LȊGHTBRINGER.** is the act of cancelling a dash by crouching, shortening the dash. SDCC costs one bar of stamina.

To SDCC, initiate a dash, then during the dash animation, quickly press the crouch key.

SDCC is more situational than other universal movement techniques, but is useful nevertheless. It is performed nearly the exact same as a Dash Slide, but duck is only temporarily held. SDCC is particularly helpful during laning to quickly Light Melee enemy troopers to confirm and deny the souls.

# Dashing/Strafe Dashing

Overview

Strafe Dashing

Dash Jumping

Dash Sliding

Short Dash Crouch Cancelling

Instant Air Dash

Ag2 Dashing

| Strafe Dashing |  |
| --- | --- |
| Load video     Local File     Local File might collect personal data.     Continue Dismiss  https://deadlock.wiki/File:Strafedash.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Hard |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Dash → (optional) Air Strafe |

**Strafe Dashing**Also known as Diagonal Dashing is any air dash in which you dash at an angle to your current velocity. There are multiple different ways of Strafe Dashing, suited for different scenarios.

When dashing normally, your directional speed is the dot product of your velocity and air dash direction. Your directional speed is capped by a speed cap of a base of ~700 u/s and ~900 with the  Vitality Item  Stamina Mastery (** **3,600****).

The speed cap limits the speed you can head in and hampers movement, but only applies to movement in the same direction as your current velocity. By dashing at an angle to your current velocity, your air dash will add to your speed beyond the speed cap. This is called a Strafe Dash.

When under the speed cap, Strafe Dashing has a minimal effect. When over the speed cap, Strafe Dashing helps alleviate the slowdown when dashing forwards.

Strafe Dashing can be done two ways:

- *Sideways*

- By turning to an angle then dashing to the side in the opposite direction, you can execute a Strafe Dash. By doing this, you will not need to air strafe back to your intended direction, since you are now heading in that direction. This method is more suited for higher speeds, such as when using Zipline Momentum Cancel.
- *Forwards*

- By turning to an angle then dashing forwards, then air strafing back to a forward direction, you can execute a Strafe Dash. The air strafe does not add speed; it only redirects you in the correct direction. This method is better suited for lower speeds, such as from a walk.

The optimal angle to Strafe Dash depends on your current velocity:

- At lower speeds, an angle of ~50 degrees is optimal.
- From a base dash jump, an angle of ~45 degrees is optimal.
- At higher speeds, make the air dash angle closer to perpendicular for the optimal Strafe Dash.

# Deadlock

*Deadlock'*s logo.

***Deadlock*** is a 6v6 third-person shooter MOBA developed by Valve Corporation.[1] It was first publicly announced on August 23, 2024.[2] The official website is https://www.playdeadlock.com/. The game's release was unconventional and marked by a deliberate approach of secrecy before public acknowledgement. The game can only be played by receiving an invite from a Steam friend who already has the game. The game is still in development and is played through a Closed Beta[3] Early Development Build.[2]

## Contents

- 1 Gameplay
- 2 Setting & Theme
- 3 Development
- 4 Invites

- 4.1 Official forums
- 5 Gallery
- 6 References

## Gameplay

[edit | edit source]

*Main article: Mechanics*

In *Deadlock*, two teams of 6 players, The Hidden King and The Archmother, battle through 3 lanes of New York. Each team fights on behalf of a god, called a Patron. The objective is to destroy the enemy's Patron while defending your own to complete the ritual. Players control Heroes with upgradable abilities, and items are bought using souls. Souls are earned by defeating enemies and completing tasks. They can also unlock 'boons' from Patrons, which boost Hero stats.

Heroes level up, unlock abilities, and equip Weapon, Vitality, and Spirit items in slots. Additional Flex slots are unlocked by completing objectives.

The game blends elements of shooters and MOBAs. It focuses on tactics, teamwork, and strategy, with third-person skill shots, movement, and gunplay. It also has a unique zipline system for long-distance transportation.

In addition to the standard gamemode, Deadlock also offers a 4v4 roguelike gamemode called Street Brawl, where players fight in one lane over short rounds.

## Setting & Theme

[edit | edit source]

*Main article: Lore*

In the world of *Deadlock,* occult rituals and magic anomalies are part of everyday life. The game takes place in an alternate version of early 20th century New York called The Cursed Apple. Two covenants battle to complete the Ritual and summon their Patron, a god capable of granting wishes. Each character has their own wishes and reason for wanting to summon the Patron, and their fates collide on the streets of New York. The game's setting is an urban fantasy with strong occult themes and elements of noir, gothic, and dieselpunk fiction.

## Development

[edit | edit source]

*Deadlock* was originally meant to be a sci-fi third-person MOBA called *Neon Prime.* It was also known as *Citadel,* *Project8* and *Shadowline* at various points in its early development. Valve trademarked *Neon Prime* in October 2022,[4] but the game was renamed to *Deadlock* later that year*.*

The currently ongoing *Deadlock* closed playtest began on April 2024,[5] when the official forums and Discord server were created, and the name was trademarked by Valve on May 2024.[6] The game was leaked on various occasions from 2019 to 2024, and Valve listed the game on Steam in August 2024.

While *Deadlock* hasn't been officially mentioned or promoted by Valve beyond its Steam page, various Valve employees, contractors and voice actors have acknowledged their work on the game on social media, and it was mentioned in the *Half-Life 2* anniversary documentary on November 2024.[7]

## Invites

[edit | edit source]

Any player with access to *Deadlock* can invite an unlimited number of Steam friends.

Here are recommended resources to get an invite:

- Deadlock Steam forums
- Reddit r/DeadlockTheGame invite megathread

- Deadlock Community Discord invite thread

An invite can take minutes to hours to be processed, and has to be accepted by the player. If the invite notification doesn't appear after a few hours, check your Steam playtest invites. If a player has refused an invite in the past, they may be unable to receive a new one.

### Official forums

[edit | edit source]

Once a player has joined the game, they can click the "give feedback" button in the main menu to create a forum account and join the official Discord server. Please note that the Discord link is one use only.

# Death

“

This won't be the end.

— Victor

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Music_stinger_player_death.mp3Music stinger for the player's death.

**Death** occurs when a hero takes sufficient damage to be reduced to zero health. Upon dying, the player's screen is shaded gray, a death timer is displayed over their hero's icon, souls are rewarded to heroes who earned a kill or an assist, and other hero or situation-specific events may occur, as detailed below.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Respawn Time

- 2.1 Comeback kill
- 2.2 Last Stand Buff
- 2.3 Rejuvenator Crystal Revive Tokens
- 3 Update history
- 4 Trivia

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Upon dying, heroes will drop any of their unsecured souls in a spherical container that can then be picked up by other heroes.

While dead, players can browse the shop, spectate their teammates, use pings and talk in chat. If all allies are dead, only the Patron's perspective can be seen. Clicking an objective on the Minimap allows the player to view the perspective of that objective.

Once the countdown reaches zero, heroes will respawn back in base.

## Respawn Time

[edit | edit source]

Example of a respawn timer
https://deadlock.wiki/File:Music_stinger_player_respawn_countdown.mp3Music stinger played before the end of respawn countdown.
https://deadlock.wiki/File:Music_stinger_player_respawn.mp3Music stinger played when the player respawns

As the game progresses, the players will take longer to respawn. The respawn time increases linearly based on the following times:

| Match duration | Respawn time |
| --- | --- |
| Start | 8s |
| 19 min | 30s |
| 30 min | 70s |
| 40 min | 85s |

The respawn time is capped at 85s.

Dying to a non-player Unit (when there is no bounty/assist from an enemy Hero) will increase the respawn time by 10s.

### Comeback kill

[edit | edit source]

After 10 minutes in a match, killing a player whose net worth is above 15% higher than the killer team's average net worth increases that player's respawn time. The increase varies based on the net worth difference and match duration, from +6s for 15% net worth at 10 minutes to +22s for 30% net worth at 25 minutes.

### Last Stand Buff

[edit | edit source]

Killing the first stage of a Patron shortens the remaining respawn time of any dead player in the defending team, as follows:

- If the remaining time is 30s or above, it is shortened by 20s (e.g. 45s shortened to 25s);
- If it's between 10s and 30s, it is shortened to 10s;
- At 10s and below, the respawn time is unchanged.

This effect is only applied once, at the moment the Patron is killed. Subsequent deaths will have the regular respawn time.

### Rejuvenator Crystal Revive Tokens

[edit | edit source]

Revive Tokens are obtained from the Crystal that drops upon killing the Mid-Boss. The Crystal contains a total of 3 Revive Tokens.

Revive Tokens can only be claimed by a Heavy Melee, and only 1 is granted per punch.

Revive Tokens are consumed upon a players death, and any further deaths from that player will not consume more. Once all the Tokens are consumed, the entire team will lose access to the mid-boss buff.

Killing a player with a Rejuvenator credit does not appear as a kill in the HUD and does not grant any souls, but it does trigger "on hero kill" effects such as the cooldown reset of  Shiv's  Killing Blow or the stack buildup of  Grey Talon's,  Mo & Krill's and  Vindicta's ultimates. The same happens when triggering  Victor's  Shocking Reanimation.

[edit | edit source]

# Debuff Resist

Debuff Resist is a stat which reduces the length of time negative effects affect a hero.

This stat is gained in the form of a percentage. As an example, "30% Debuff Resist" will reduce the duration of a 10 second debuff by 3 seconds.

Debuff Resist can be gained by purchasing specific items at the Shop.
